Migrants are to be given high-visibility vests in Piddington – the village which is today holding a symbolic independence referendum over a nearby asylum seekers camp – to stop them getting hit by cars.
As residents went to the polls today, the Government revealed the plans for the high-vis garments – saying they are part of a safety drive to stop new arrivals being hit on ‘death trap’ roads near the Oxfordshire village.
Piddington, which has just 350 residents, is fighting back against plans to convert a former Ministry of Defence garrison into a camp for 1,250 male migrants. Today’s referendum will decide whether the village should remain part of the UK.
Cabinet minister Jonathan Reynolds defended the migrant camp move this morning, saying every part of the country must be prepared to take in asylum seekers.
The plans will mean women are outnumbered around ten to one by male asylum seekers, raising safety concerns amid a wave of sex crimes perpetrated by boat migrants elsewhere in recent years.
But villagers have also warned that the plans make little practical sense, as the roads to and from the former MoD site do not have any pavements so migrants could end up posing a significant road safety risk.
Government officials have tried to head off these concerns by claiming that ‘high visibility vests will be provided to those leaving on foot’, according to planning documents.
Piddington's women are campaigning against plans to house 1,250 asylum seekers near their village
The people of Piddington are off to the polls today
Reform's Suella Braverman has backed the residents' fight
Migrants will be ‘strongly encouraged’ to only use the provided shuttle buses at the camp but, since authorities have no power to actually stop people leaving on foot, the vests will be handed out ‘to further emphasise the potential danger’.
Piddington resident Ian Darby, 63, told the Daily Mail it was just one of many reasons the former military base was ill-suited to housing so many migrants.
‘If they go wandering, they don’t have pavements on that road,’ he said. ‘It’s very dangerous. The Government says they are going to issue high-vis jackets, but the widest pathway is just one metre. It’s a death trap.’
The surrounding roads have a 50mph speed limit, with the planning documents accepting the military site ‘lacks safe/pavemented routes’ and ‘to enter or exit to site on foot would require considerable care’.
The village's 350 residents organised today's symbolic vote on whether to leave the UK after ministers ignored their pleas not to move single male migrants into the nearby military camp at Bicester.
If the camp reaches capacity, asylum seekers will outnumber local residents by almost four to one. Asylum seekers will be free to leave the camp to roam freely around surrounding villages.
The result is expected to favour 'independence', with campaigners hoping the symbolic ballot will focus attention in Westminster on their concerns.
Labour is moving asylum seekers into military barracks across the country as part of its drive to end the use of hotels and reduce the cost of housing migrants.
The result of the village's referendum is expected at around 7am on Wednesday.
Members of Piddington's parish council told how they have been approached by hundreds of other British villages for advice on how to replicate the campaign, sparking speculation that such referendums could spread across the country.
Reform UK leader Nigel Farage subsequently vowed to support any areas that want to hold similar votes.
Labour politicians are yet to clarify how long the military camp will house the asylum seekers.
Ahead of the vote, locals have told how they are terrified by the plans.
More than 20 women said they have signed up for self-defence classes after they were reportedly urged to 'take precautions' by police ahead of the migrants' arrival.

items.body_text:
Lucy Letby inquiry - latest: Two babies murdered by nurse could have been saved
Serial killer Letby, 36, was convicted of killing seven babies and attempting to murder seven more, with two attempts on one of those victims
An inquiry into the crimes of killer nurse Lucy Letby - who was convicted of killing seven babies and attempting to murder seven more - has found some of the tragic deaths could have been avoided if hospital staff had acted differently.
A scathing report has found there was a "complete failure to protect babies" at the Countess of Chester Hospital where Letby, now 36, worked between 2015 and 2016. It found that, if action had been taken, with Letby moved off the ward, then the deaths of babies referred to as O and P would not have occurred, and neither would attacks on babies J, K, L, M and N
Lady Justice Thirlwall, who chaired the inquiry, said no-one at the hospital seems to have understood "that safeguarding action is required when a member of staff is suspected of causing deliberate harm and does not require colleagues to be sure of guilt". She added that the "lack of consideration shown to parents" by hospital management was "reprehensible".
The report found that senior nurses never accepted concerns from consultants about Letby were - or might be - justified and that there was a delay in senior management calling the police.
Letby was found to have killed and harmed babies by injecting air into their blood, poisoning them with insulin, and overfeeding them with milk.
Key Events
Lucy Letby's lawyer issues fiery statement after two top experts quit hours before inquiry verdict
Lucy Letby's lawyer has insisted her campaign for freedom has not been undermined after two key experts quit her defence team, warning that some of her legal arguments have "fundamental, unresolvable problems”.
Engineering expert Helen Shannon and bioengineering professor Geoff Chase withdrew from the team on Monday, raising concerns about legal arguments put forward by Letby’s team.
Video: Lady Justice Thirlwall recommends baby monitors on cots and incubators
Lady Justice Thirlwall has recommended that all cots and incubators in all neonatal units should be fitted with in-cot cameras with livestreaming video to try and prevent anything like the events at the Countess of Chester Hospital ever happening again.
Inquiry recommendations: CQC assessment, ombudsman, implementation
Lady Justice Thirlwall has made 17 recommendations in her report.
- Assessment of the performance of CQC. There must be a rigorous and consistent review and assessment of the performance of CQC by the Health and Social Care Committee.
- Parliamentary and Health Service Ombudsman. The functions of the National Guardian’s Office should be taken over by the Parliamentary and Health Service Ombudsman in England. The Ombudsman’s powers must be increased to include: investigating complaints that whistleblowing in the NHS has not been dealt with adequately and assisting whistleblowers by referring their concerns to the relevant NHS bodies.
- Implementation of recommendations. Responsibility for auditing the implementation of the recommendations of statutory inquiries into NHS bodies should be given to the National Audit Office.
Inquiry recommendations part 4 of 5: medical examiners, pathologists and accountability
Lady Justice Thirlwall has made 17 recommendations in her report.
- Medical examiners. There should be standardised national guidance on dealing with the death of a newborn. Medical examiners should ask direct questions of the attending practitioner as to whether there is a concern that a child has been harmed or some other safeguarding concern and record details of all medics who attended the baby. There should be a pool of neonatologists who can assist medical examiners until regional neonatologist medical examiners can be appointed. The medical examiner system should be reviewed again in 2027 by the government to see if there is enough funding.

items.title: Crypto billionaires hand Reform more than 10 times what Labour gets from unions
items.summary: Donations from crypto billionaires to Reform UK amount to more than 10 times the funding Labour has received from unions, analysis of official data shows
items.body_text:
Crypto billionaires hand Reform more than 10 times what Labour gets from unions
Donations from crypto billionaires to Reform UK amount to more than 10 times the funding Labour has received from unions, analysis of official data shows
Donations from crypto billionaires to Reform UK amount to more than 10 times the funding Labour has received from unions, analysis of official data shows.
More than half of all political donations since the last election have been made to Reform UK. The party made headlines this weekend when it was revealed that they had received two record-breaking donations from their biggest donors.
Christopher Harborne and Ben Delo have each given the party £36million, making them the joint single largest donations in British political history. They eclipsed the previous record of £10million made by Lord John Sainsbury to the Conservative Party in September 2023.
But the latest donations may fall foul of incoming changes to the law that would restrict donations from expats to £100,000. Mr Delo and Mr Harborne's gifts are likely to be affected by the new rules, as they came into effect on March 25, when they were announced.
You can see the donations received by each party since the last general election by using our interactive chart:
If Reform has to hand back the cash, Nigel Farage has threatened to cut off Labour's union funding if his right-wing outfit ever wins power. In an article for The Telegraph, he said: "I would just warn the Labour Party here and now: if you try and ban our donors, we in government would certainly ban funding from the trade unions. I don't want to go down that route. But it is something we would be prepared to do."
Labour’s largest donations since the election have tended to be from the unions. A total of £9million has been received by the party from a variety of different unions.
Reform has received more than 10-times that amount from crypto billionaires, with the latest donations pushing the total to £95million from Christopher Harborne and Ben Delo.
Unite the Union has given £2.7million since July 2024. GMB, meanwhile, has donated £1.8million, Union of Shop Distributive and Allied Workers (USDAW) has given £1.8million, UNISON has given £1.6million, while Gary Lubner has given just under £1.4million.
Since the last general election, Reform UK has now received almost £107million. That’s more than half (55%) of all money given to parties in that time, including public funds.
Data from the Electoral Commission shows every donation received by political parties up to the end of June this year.
Reform UK had received almost a third (28%) of all donations up to that point. The newly announced £72million dwarfs the amount received by their rivals and is far more than The Conservatives (£37million), Labour (£21million), Lib Dems (£17million), SNP (£2million) and Green (£2million) combined.
The Conservative Party have received their largest contribution from public funds.
The House of Commons has given the party almost £9.1million in central funding since the last election. Games software magnate, Jeremy Elliott San, has given the party £3.0million. The National Conservative Draws Society £1.4million, the House of Lords £1.3 million, the House of Commons Fees Office £1.3million, and Mary V Doran £1.1million.
Broaden the timeframe, however, and we see the traditional parties receiving more money. In the whole of 2024, Labour received £42million. The bulk of that (£32million) was in the months leading up to the general election.
The Conservatives received £32million that year, and £48million in 2023.
Reform UK have now received almost £110million since the start of 2021. The Conservatives have received £150million in that time, Labour have received £129million, the Lib Dems £45million, and the Greens £5million.

items.title: Video of ‘zombie’ Mitch McConnell returning to the Senate causes internet uproar and raises more questions
items.summary: Mitch McConnell returned to Capitol Hill to cast a vote — his first public appearance in months
items.body_text:
Video of ‘zombie’ Mitch McConnell returning to the Senate causes internet uproar and raises more questions
Mitch McConnell returned to Capitol Hill to cast a vote — his first public appearance in months
- Bookmark
- CommentsGo to comments
Former Senate GOP leader Mitch McConnell’s return to Capitol Hill — his first public appearance in months — sent the Internet into a tizzy as footage showed the senator spacing out in a way commentators deemed zombie-like.
The 84-year-old Kentucky Republican has faced intense media scrutiny and questions about his ability to serve after he was hospitalized in mid-June following a fall and a mild case of pneumonia. He remained hospitalized, and later in a rehab center, for weeks until he was discharged in August.
However, he returned to cast a vote Monday when the chamber decided on a nomination to fill an opening on a district court bench in Ohio.
In a statement, McConnell described his recovery as “a long and often frustrating process,” and said that while he is not “quite back to 100%,” he will “do my best to be present for tough votes when our Conference needs me.”
Despite his attempts to reassure the public, footage TMZ published on Monday of McConnell in a car arriving on Capitol Hill with his mouth agape raised concerns about his ability to work.
“Mitch looks like he is a zombie being remotely controlled. This is SO STRANGE!!!! Is he even alive?” one X user commented.
“Mitch McConnell is the deadest alive person,” another X user chimed in.
“They’re Weekend at Bernie’s-ing him,” one X user joked.
Another X user commented: “It’s actually terrifying that Mitch McConnell gets to make decisions that affect all of us.”
Right-wing provocateur Laura Loomer also weighed in, writing on X, “Like I said, Mitch is brain dead.”
“You can’t look at his face and say he’s not a vegetable. He’s not even responding to cognition tests. It’s like wheeling a corpse around. Worse than what the Democrats did with Joe Biden to be honest. He looks incapcitated. Brain dead,” she said.
Questions about McConnell’s health and ability to serve have swirled around Washington, D.C., ever since he was hospitalized earlier this summer following a fall. He said he later suffered from pneumonia after his initial hospitalization.
At the time, Kentucky’s Democratic governor, Andy Beshear, repeatedly called on McConnell to release a video statement confirming his ability to return to work, but was rebuffed. The senator’s office released a photo of him and his wife, former Transportation Secretary Elaine Chao, in late July amidst the continued calls for proof of his recovery progress.
McConnell has suffered several falls on Capitol Hill over the past few years. The senator, who suffered from childhood polio, has used a wheelchair in the past — as well as on Monday. Footage showed him being wheeled out to a waiting car on Monday in front of a crowd of spectators.
He was driven to the Senate, where he made a brief statement and did not take questions from journalists.
McConnell, who retired as leader of the GOP Senate caucus in January 2025, announced last year that he would not seek re-election, and will exit the Senate at the end of this year.

items.title: Fashion CEO apologizes after restraining two protestors at New York Fashion Week event
items.summary: ‘There is no justification for physically restraining another person,’ the CEO writes
items.body_text:
Fashion CEO apologizes after restraining two protestors at New York Fashion Week event
‘There is no justification for physically restraining another person,’ the CEO writes
- Bookmark
- CommentsGo to comments
A fashion CEO has apologized after restraining two protesters at a New York Fashion Week show.
Steven Kolb, the CEO and President of the Council of Fashion Designers, grabbed a protester at the COS fashion show on Sunday. Footage released by PETA showed Kolb gripping a protester by his face, appearing to cover his mouth as he shouted a slogan.
The video also shows Kolb dragging a female protester to the ground, before clamping a hand over her mouth. Then, while sitting down, Kolb appears to place a leg over her body.
“My actions were wrong, and I am deeply sorry. I take full responsibility for my actions,” Kolb wrote on his Instagram story, “I take full responsibility for my actions. I apologize to them and to everyone who witnessed the incident.”
Kolb added, “There is no justification for physically restraining another person. Security should have handled the situation, and I should have stepped back.”
The CEO has since been placed on leave from the CFDA, which hosts New York Fashion Week. It is launching a review into the incident.
“The CFDA takes this matter very seriously and, as a result, Mr Kolb will be on leave pending review,” a spokesperson told The New York Times. “The CFDA as an organization is committed to working with dissenting voices to find commonality and is engaged in efforts to move the American fashion industry forward while upholding the values of our membership.”
In his apology, Kolb described his leave as “voluntary” and said that he was meeting with a “professional to ensure it never happens again.”
“What happened was completely out of character for me, both personally and as a leader,” he wrote.
In a post on Facebook, PETA revealed that the protest was focused on conditions endured by sheep in the wool industry.
“He spoke out for sheep who are forcibly restrained, roughly shorn, and ultimately sent to slaughter for wool - then experienced violent restraint himself,” the organization wrote, referring to the protester.
The organization, which was founded in 1980 and campaigns for animal rights issues, also asked Kolb to watch footage allegedly detailing abuse endured by sheep.
“Now, we're asking Kolb to meet with us and watch footage from our 17 wool industry exposés that document the abuse sheep endure,” a PETA spokesperson wrote.
On his Instagram story, Kolb apologized again and said that he hopes to be able to apologize to those whom he restrained.
“I have accepted an invitation from PETA to meet and discuss their concerns, and I hope to have the opportunity to apologize in person to the two individuals who did not deserve that treatment,” he wrote.
During Kolb’s tenure as CEO, the CFDA announced it was banning the use of fur in any collections featured on New York Fashion Week’s schedule. At the time, Kolb cheered the move.
“There is already little to no fur shown at NYFW, but by taking this position, the CFDA hopes to inspire American designers to think more deeply about the fashion industry’s impact on animals,” Kolb wrote.
According to his Substack account, he also follows a vegetarian diet.
The Independent has contacted H&M Group, which owns COS, and the CFDA for comment.

items.title: Exclusive: Cheesecake Factory guest with severe peanut allergy sues over meal ‘smothered in peanut sauce’
items.summary: Caylin Tucker, 22, was out to dinner with her parents when she began to go into anaphylactic shock, according to a state lawsuit filed in Houston, Texas
items.body_text:
Exclusive: Cheesecake Factory guest with severe peanut allergy sues over meal ‘smothered in peanut sauce’
Caylin Tucker, 22, was out to dinner with her parents when she began to go into anaphylactic shock, according to a state lawsuit filed in Houston, Texas
- Bookmark
A Cheesecake Factory patron with a severe peanut allergy went into anaphylactic shock after taking a bite of a dish she was assured would be peanut-free but came out of the kitchen “smothered in peanut sauce,” according to a lawsuit obtained by The Independent.
In a civil complaint filed September 11 in Harris County District Court, Caylin Tucker, 22, says she was out to dinner with her parents last June when the “preventable incident” occurred.
The three were at a Cheesecake Factory in the Houston area, and before ordering, Tucker “let her waiter… know that she has a severe peanut allergy and would like to be sure her meal does not contain peanuts.”
“The waiter assured [Tucker] that her meal could be made without peanuts,” the complaint continues.
However, when Tucker took the first bite, she “immediately noticed” that the dish “contained peanuts and was smothered in peanut sauce,” the complaint goes on. It claims Tucker felt her tongue and lips start to swell, after which her throat started to close up amid the onset of anaphylaxis.
As Tucker struggled to breathe, she broke out in hives, the complaint continues. Cheesecake Factory employees began apologizing to Tucker upon realizing the gravity of the situation, according to the complaint.
Anaphylaxis is an allergic reaction that shuts down the body’s airways and can be fatal without immediate medical intervention. For some, it can come on quickly, without warning. In one instance highlighted by the Mayo Clinic, a 20-year-old woman with a shellfish allergy nearly died from an anaphylactic reaction that occurred shortly after she kissed her boyfriend, who had eaten shrimp earlier that day.
Tucker “required emergency medical treatment and incurred substantial medical expenses,” the complaint states. It says she also suffered “physical pain, mental anguish, emotional distress, physical impairment, inconvenience and other damages.”
The complaint does not specify the dish that Tucker ordered, or whether or not the peanut sauce was visible to her before she started eating. It also does not say if she had an EpiPen with her – a self-administered dose of epinephrine, which can buy precious time for someone in anaphylaxis – or if she was taken to the hospital. Tucker’s attorney did not respond on Monday to messages seeking further details.
Tucker’s complaint blames the Cheesecake Factory and the unnamed server for promising, but failing to deliver, a meal without peanuts.
Further, the complaint claims the Cheesecake Factory breached its duty to “exercise ordinary care in the preparation, inspection, handling and service of food.”
Among other things, it says the chain and the individual employees in question failed to abide by proper allergen-safety protocols, failed to properly communicate Tucker’s order to kitchen staff and failed to warn Tucker of “the presence of peanuts” in her food.
The complaint also criticizes the Cheesecake Factory, which is known for its near-endless menu and gargantuan portions, for allegedly failing to train employees on “how to properly document customers’ allergies,” and, “how to properly check the food before giving it to customers.”
Tucker bears no responsibility for what happened to her, the complaint contends. Instead, it claims the Cheesecake factory is the one ultimately responsible for the “acts and omissions of its employees,” including the kitchen staff who prepared Tucker’s food, and the server who brought it to her.
Food safety issues involving the Cheesecake Factory, which did not respond to a request for comment, are uncommon but not unheard of.

items.title: What Andrew-Epstein police will examine next as they appeal to protection officers
items.summary: Investigators are working their way through evidence as ex-palace protection officer claims his testimony has been ignored
items.body_text:
The Metropolitan Police is continuing to contact royal protection officers who may have worked with Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor following claims they may have information relevant to Jeffrey Epstein-linked investigations.
It comes after a former protection officer sent a dossier of evidence on the former prince to the FBI, claiming he had been ignored by British police.
Paul Page, who was based at Buckingham Palace between 1998 and 2004, claimed Mountbatten-Windsor breached security rules to bring women into the palace.
Shorts
Ex-protection officer’s claims
Page – who was convicted of a £3m property scam in 2009 – previously told The i Paper that officers were instructed to ensure official visitor logs did not record the names of Mountbatten-Windsor’s guests.
He said he had seen up to three women walking in and out of Mountbatten-Windsor’s residence in a single night while he was working there.
His claims have so far not been corroborated, and the former duke of York has repeatedly denied any wrongdoing.
Page also sent his testimony to US congressman Thomas Massie, who earlier this month called for Mountbatten-Windsor to be investigated and prosecuted for sex crimes in the US.
Police examining ‘significant’ amount of information
It is not clear how Page’s claims will be treated by UK and US law enforcement, if at all.
Both the Met and Thames Valley Police – which is investigating whether Mountbatten-Windsor passed confidential and official Government documents to Epstein as trade envoy – declined to go into specifics.
The FBI and US Department of Justice did not respond to a request for comment.
However, former Met officer Graham Wettone said investigators would review any information they receive in order of priority.
“In my experience, any witness that comes forward with what is potentially relevant viable evidence will be assessed, will be looked at. It’s done in a priority order, it’s done in a relevance order, as in, ‘Is this one of our key objectives or priorities at this stage of the investigation?'” he said.
“It depends at what stage the investigation is at when he [Page] gets spoken to. The fact they haven’t spoken to one person yet doesn’t mean to say they are being ignored. It’s just that whatever they put in hasn’t chronologically been addressed yet.”
Wettone added: “There’s clearly a wide range of people that need to be spoken to, including other retired police officers, people who have who have closer links to Andrew.”
A Met spokesperson said: “The Met is continuing to make written contact with former and serving officers who we understand may have worked closely, in a protection capacity, with Andrew Mountbatten‑Windsor. They have been asked to consider carefully whether anything they saw or heard during that period of service may be relevant to our ongoing reviews and to share any information that could assist us.
“Should any new allegations come to light they will be assessed in the usual way.”
A Thames Valley Police spokesperson said: “Our experienced team is working meticulously through a significant amount of information. While we cannot go into specific details of our investigation, we are following all reasonable lines of enquiry.”
Nationwide review of Andrew and Epstein files
Three British police forces – Thames Valley, the Met and Surrey – are running live investigations linked to the Epstein files.
The Met is leading a misconduct in public office investigation into Peter Mandelson, the former British ambassador to the US, amid claims that he leaked market-sensitive material to Epstein while serving as business secretary. Mandelson has denied any wrongdoing.
Following the further release of millions of Epstein-related documents by the US Department of Justice, the force has also launched a review of suggestions that London airports may have been used to facilitate human trafficking and sexual exploitation.
Thames Valley Police arrested Mountbatten-Windsor in February on suspicion of misconduct in public

items.title: The coded message behind Harry and Meghan’s children moving school after two days
items.summary: Anne McElvoy: Harry and his legal team have seen a grain of legal argument to work with here
items.body_text:
It’s only a day since a perky Instagram reel displayed the upbeat vibes from the Duke and Duchess of Sussex’s Cotswolds hideaway, showing the happy family on a muddy English walk and introducing the British public to at least the back view of their two energetic children.
Today, it’s a different and more sombre story. The couple has pulled their children from school after only two days in the new term over “security concerns” about their commute, ranging from heavy school-run traffic and the distance between their home – chosen for optimal privacy – and the schools, as well as operational difficulties for their bodyguards trying to convoy Archie and Lilibet to school safely.
Much of this boils down to practicalities – school runs in the well-heeled English countryside are just busy, in the way that Sheffield Drive in Montecito, the couple’s California home for the past years, gets busy.
And some of this could have been anticipated. A private school, chosen because it had a free-wheeling, outdoorsy ethos, was never going to be as well-guarded as an urban educational fortress. Oxfordshire is not the Golden State, despite the proliferation of luxury 4x4s on the roads and high-end temporary American residents.
The couple did thank the school warmly for its attentiveness to avoid any sense that they were flouncing away. Yet, the bigger picture here is one which matters hugely to the Sussexes – and that’s where they feel they can secure an overdue win against their detractors.
That is about their status under the VIP protection arrangements, a longstanding bone of contention for the Duke. That’s the purview of the Home Office committee Ravec – Executive Committee for the Protection of Royalty and Public Figures – which makes dispensations about the level taxpayer funded security can be justified for royals and other prominent individuals.
Now the committee has written to the couple, initiating a new “risk assessment” for both the Duke and Duchess. Crucially, as the couple insist they are here in the UK for a lengthy if unspecified period, they escape the situation which angered Harry previously – under which the committee, which features members from the royal household, judged the Sussexes not to meet a threshold for official protection because they were fleetingly in the UK and had an irregular pattern of visits.
That, I am told, fell well short of a “pattern of life” assessment which needs to be conducted to establish access to full security protection – which is not a cheap affair.
A new risk assessment is a concession by the committee and it must be said that it has occurred because Harry, who has a Jarndyce v Jarndyce level of commitment to lengthy legal cases and appeals, has changed one important factor here by moving to the UK with his wife and family. The school-run anxieties and foregrounding the security risks of convoys on busy roads duly boosts the couple’s claim that they should have a higher level of protection, because the risks cannot otherwise be sensibly dealt with.
In more “political” terms, the security issue is a lever which the Duke and Duchess can deploy, based on their status in public life and prominence.
Harry and his legal team have seen a grain of legal argument to work with here: while the court of appeal upheld the original court decision not to fund protection for the couple when they were infrequently in the UK, it pointed out that in terms of rights to protection “the Prince had left the cohort of individuals automatically protected by Ravec when he stepped back from official duties, but he re-entered that protective cohort under bespoke terms for his visits to the UK”.
So, while Harry lost previous security battles and an appeal, he believes that he will win the security war.

items.title: The five most important findings from Lucy Letby inquiry – and what it means for her
items.summary: The £18.5m public inquiry found 'a complete failure to protect babies' on the neonatal unit at the Countess of Chester Hospital
items.body_text:
At least three babies could have been saved from Britain’s worst child serial killer Lucy Letby if action had been taken sooner, a public inquiry has found.
Lady Justice Thirlwall said there was “a complete failure to protect babies on the neonatal unit at the Countess of Chester Hospital”, while Letby was harming newborns in 2015 and 2016.
Letby, 36, is currently serving fifteen whole life orders for the murder of seven babies and attempting to murder a further seven.
Shorts
During two trials, prosecutors said former neonatal nurse Letby harmed babies by poisoning them with insulin, injecting them with air and milk and causing physical trauma.
Letby has always maintained her innocence, but has twice had applications to overturn her convictions rejected by High Court judges.
The independent body the Criminal Cases Review Commission (CCRC) is the only remaining option for her to challenge her convictions and it is currently considering a fresh application.
1. At least three babies could have been saved
Lady Thirlwall said that no real safeguarding action began until after the death of Baby I in October 2015.
Even then, Letby was not moved off the ward.
If she had, the deaths of Baby O and Baby P and the attacks on Babies J, K, L, and M between November 2015 and June 2016 would not have occurred, the report found.
Lady Thirlwall added that it is “possible” Letby could have been caught even earlier in August 2015. A medic known as Dr ZA had “disregarded” a result which showed abnormal levels of insulin in a baby after they had been poisoned.
If this had resulted in safeguarding action, the attacks on Babies G, H and the death of Baby I would not have occurred.
2. Whistleblower doctors ‘deprived of protection’
Letby was eventually moved off the ward and Cheshire Police called in after a prolonged period of disagreement between nurses, doctors and senior management about why babies were suffering unexpected collapses and dying.
Lady Thirlwall said that from the first meeting about the increase in baby deaths in June 2015, there was a “them and us” approach between nurses and doctors which should not have occurred and “distracted from the real issue”.
Doctors who did eventually speak out about their concerns with Letby were not protected by hospital managers and were even threatened with referral to regulators.
“Despite raising concerns in good faith, the consultants were deprived of protection from recrimination,” Lady Thirlwall said.
3. ‘Repeated failures’ from ‘foolhardy’ senior managers
There was also a lack of oversight from senior managers.
In September 2015, a meeting of the hospital’s Board of Directors said that the most senior doctor, medical director Ian Harvey, “personally” reviewed all deaths at the hospital.
Harvey admitted in evidence to the Thirlwall inquiry this wasn’t true and that, in fact, he reviewed only adult deaths, not those involving children.
Lady Thirlwall said that senior managers “repeatedly failed in the duty of candour in their dealings with the bereaved parents, investigators, or regulatory organisations”.
She said their behaviour was “high-handed, contrary to all safeguarding principles and foolhardy”.
Following Letby’s convictions, Cheshire Police launched a separate corporate manslaughter investigation and three former executives have been arrested. No charges have yet been brought.
4. Treatment of parents was ‘reprehensible’
Many parents of the babies who were harmed by Letby also tried to raise concerns – mainly about the poor care they felt they had received – but were ignored.
They were not informed when the hospital made important decisions, such as bringing in the police, and their children’s medical records were shared without their consent, the inquiry said.
Parents who gave evidence “took the view that protecting the reputation of the hospital was more important to senior managers than keeping them informed about what was the happening”, the inquiry said.

items.title: DOE calls for stronger global action to protect ozone layer, tackle climate change
items.summary: TEHRAN – Shina Ansari, the head of the Department of Environment, has called for stronger international cooperation to address the harmful effects of ozone-layer depletion and climate change, saying that global participation, strong commitment to obligations, and dedicated financial resources can produce real, tangible, measurable, and monitorable results.
items.body_text:
DOE calls for stronger global action to protect ozone layer, tackle climate change
TEHRAN – Shina Ansari, the head of the Department of Environment, has called for stronger international cooperation to address the harmful effects of ozone-layer depletion and climate change, saying that global participation, strong commitment to obligations, and dedicated financial resources can produce real, tangible, measurable, and monitorable results.
Speaking at a ceremony on Tuesday, marking World Ozone Day, she said, “We have gathered today to reaffirm our commitment to fully restoring and rebuilding the Earth’s protective shield and safeguarding life against harmful solar radiation. We must take more effective steps toward our shared goals of addressing global environmental challenges, both in protecting the ozone layer and in mitigating global warming.”
Referring to the Montreal Protocol, Ansari said it is a global agreement aimed at controlling the production, trade, and consumption of chemicals that deplete the ozone layer, with the ultimate goal of protecting life on Earth through the gradual phase-out of ozone-depleting substances.
The official added that the landmark agreement, adopted in 1987 and entering into force in 1989, is now regarded as one of the world’s most successful environmental agreements and an inspiring model for environmental cooperation.
“Thanks to the joint efforts of countries around the world, the ozone layer is currently on a path toward recovery and restoration, and significant progress has been made in this regard,” she said.
The protocol has demonstrated that science-based policymaking, global participation, effective international cooperation, strong commitment to obligations, and dedicated financial resources can produce real, tangible, measurable, and monitorable results, Ansari noted.
She added that this process has not only made ozone-layer protection possible but has also enabled countries and industries to move toward safer, more environmentally friendly alternatives while supporting economic development.
Kigali Amendment
Referring to the Kigali Amendment, Ansari said this year marks the 10th anniversary of the amendment, the latest amendment to the Montreal Protocol, which was adopted to gradually reduce global emissions of powerful greenhouse gases known as hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs) and accelerate the transition to more efficient and safer refrigerants.
Over the past decade, implementation of the amendment in various countries has demonstrated how the promotion of efficient technologies, the strengthening of industrial capacity, and support for innovation in the refrigeration sector can help advance development priorities, she said.
Ansari predicted that full implementation of the amendment could prevent between 0.5 and 1 degree Celsius of global warming by 2100, describing it as one of the most important approaches to mitigating climate change in the present century.
She said that, in line with the protocol’s new objectives of aligning ozone-layer protection with efforts to reduce global warming, issues such as new technologies, increased energy efficiency, equipment modernization, and the development of environmentally friendly technologies have been prioritized, taking into account the country’s current circumstances, economic considerations, industrial capacity, market needs, and access to safe technologies.
Given the structure of the Montreal Protocol and the cooperation of its implementing agencies and financial mechanisms, Iran can use the implementation of its international environmental commitments as an opportunity to modernize and develop domestic technology, the DOE head said.
Referring to this year’s World Ozone Day theme, “Global Action for a Cooler Planet,” Ansari said the slogan reflects the international community’s efforts to protect the ozone layer and the need to continue this path with future generations in mind.

items.title: Pezeshkian pushes for drafting Iran-China action plan to combat desertification
items.summary: TEHRAN – President Masoud Pezeshkian has highlighted the need to draft a five-year Iranian-Chinese action plan to manage airborne dust and combat desertification in line with the trilateral memorandum of understanding (MOU) signed by the two countries.
items.body_text:
Pezeshkian pushes for drafting Iran-China action plan to combat desertification
TEHRAN – President Masoud Pezeshkian has highlighted the need to draft a five-year Iranian-Chinese action plan to manage airborne dust and combat desertification in line with the trilateral memorandum of understanding (MOU) signed by the two countries.
The MOU was inked in the last month of spring in 2025, in Lanzhou, China, to promote scientific cooperation and address sand and dust storms (SDSs) challenges, IRNA reported.
Following specialized meetings and an assessment of scientific and operational indicators, a five-year action plan is scheduled to be developed, and two regions have been designated as pilot sites for implementing joint efforts.
The selected areas include Salehiyeh Wetland, a major dust source affecting Alborz, Qazvin, and Tehran provinces, and Tabas desert, another main dust hotspot in the country, chosen due to their roles in the expansion of desertification, sandstorms, and their impacts on agriculture and infrastructure.
Highlighting the importance of protecting natural resources and the environment, Pezeshkian called for taking action against unauthorized construction and illegal activities that undermine regulations and lead to environmental consequences, as well as benefiting from the capacities and expertise of the Chinese Academy of Sciences in implementing pilot projects.
The official made the remarks in a meeting held on Monday to give an account of the progress in the bilateral MOU.
Moreover, the president urged the University of Tehran to maintain constant collaboration with the Chinese Academy of Sciences and develop a joint action plan to be assessed and discussed in the next meetings. The official also asked the Plan and Budget Organization to secure funds required for the studies and measures in the five-year action plan.
Dust storms are significant environmental challenges that adversely affect food security, human health, and the sustainable development process at national and regional levels.
Being located in an arid and semi-arid area, Iran has been negatively impacted by climate change. The rise in temperatures, drop in precipitation, intensified droughts, and frequent SDSs have not only threatened the ecosystem and biodiversity but also jeopardized the country’s food security by exacerbating soil erosion, expanding desertification, and declining agricultural productivity.
Iran chairs intl. event on combating SDSs
Iran’s ambassador and permanent representative to the United Nations, Amir-Saeed Iravani, chaired a high-level event held to mark the International Day for Combating Sand and Dust Storms (SDSs) in New York on July 10.
The event was organized by the Permanent Missions of the Islamic Republic of Iran, Iraq, the Republic of Senegal and Mongolia, in cooperation with members of the United Nations Coalition on Combating Sand and Dust Storms, providing a platform to exchange experiences, strengthen partnerships and identify actions to advance implementation at the national, regional and global levels.
At Iran’s initiative, in 2023, the United Nations General Assembly proclaimed July 12 as the International Day of Combating Sand and Dust Storms, recognizing that SDSs and their negative impacts at different scales are issues of international concern.
This year, the day was marked under the theme: ‘From Source to Impact: Protecting Land and Life from Sand and Dust Storms’. The event brought together Member States, United Nations entities, regional and international organizations, experts and other stakeholders to strengthen international cooperation and accelerate action to address the growing impacts of sand and dust storms.

items.title: Islamic Republic asks public to identify opponents abroad
items.summary: The Islamic Republic has launched a platform asking citizens to identify and report opponents living abroad. Iranians met it with ridicule, pointing to how deeply the state's own security apparatus has been infiltrated.
items.body_text:
Saudi Arabia is taking a harder military posture after efforts to defuse tensions with Tehran stalled. Riyadh had sought de-escalation, wary that a wider conflict could threaten the regional stability on which its economic ambitions depend.
A meeting planned for Monday between Iran and several Persian Gulf states over arrangements for the Strait of Hormuz was postponed after Saudi Arabia requested a delay, amid Riyadh’s growing frustration over attacks by Iran-aligned groups.
That leaves Riyadh with options, none of them ideal.
Saudi Arabia does not want an all-out war. But the Houthis may be testing how long the kingdom can afford to avoid one.
Saad bin Tefla Al Ajmi, Kuwait's former information minister, said Saudi Arabia has so far exercised patience but its military options remain open.
That restraint reflects what the kingdom has at stake. Saudi Arabia has spent years trying to avoid being dragged back into direct conflict with the Houthis, while its economic transformation depends heavily on regional stability.
"There is no stability, there is no development. There is no stability, there is no prosperity," Al Ajmi told Iran International.
But Houthi attacks on Saudi territory and advances along Yemen’s Red Sea coast are making that restraint increasingly difficult to maintain. The Saudi-led coalition said Houthi missile and drone attacks on Khamis Mushait, Abha and Taif on Monday injured 13 civilians.
Al Ajmi believes some of the Houthis' recent territorial gains could be reversed, particularly if Saudi Arabia decides to deploy its overwhelming advantage in air power. He described Houthi forces operating along the flat Tihamah coastal plain as "sitting ducks."
Saudi Arabia led a military intervention against the Houthis beginning in 2015, with direct hostilities largely subsiding after a UN-brokered truce began in 2022. Years of bombardment failed to eliminate the movement, and Riyadh subsequently spent years trying to avoid being pulled back into a full-scale Yemen war.
The question now is whether the Houthis are pushing that restraint too far.
Houthis risk overplaying their hand
The battlefield in Yemen remains fluid. The Houthis have seized Mokha, Dhubab and Perim Island and expanded their control along Yemen’s Red Sea coast, while Saudi-backed government forces have regrouped and vowed to retake lost territory. That leaves open the question of how durable the Houthis’ gains will prove.
"The Houthis fought the Saudis and the Saudi militias for years. They also have a history of being overextended," Alberto Fernandez, a former senior US diplomat, told Iran International.
Fernandez said the Houthis may have pushed too far.
"I think we could see them lose some of the territory that they've gained," he said.
"They're arrogant. Yes, they're motivated by ideology. And when you're motivated by ideology and you're arrogant, you tend to sometimes overextend," Fernandez said.
But the Houthis are also betting on reluctance from both Saudi Arabia and the United States to become drawn more deeply into the conflict.
Saudi Arabia's attempt to remain outside the wider Iran war has already "certainly backfired on them," Fernandez said.
The uncertainty over how much the kingdom can rely on its allies only complicates its options.
Fernandez described the relationship between Washington and Riyadh as increasingly complicated. The Saudis, he said, felt blindsided by the United States launching the Iran war, while Washington in turn felt unsupported by Riyadh.
That strain has become more visible as Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman sought direct US military action against the Houthis, while Trump declined requests for US strikes and Washington limited its support to intelligence and targeting assistance.
That uncertainty also extends to the Makkah Joint Defense Agreement, signed by Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan on August 7. The pact says an armed attack against any one of the three countries will be regarded as an attack against all.

Saudi Arabia does not want an all-out war. But the Houthis may be testing how long the kingdom can afford to avoid one.
Saad bin Tefla Al Ajmi, Kuwait's former information minister, said Saudi Arabia has so far exercised patience but its military options remain open.
That restraint reflects what the kingdom has at stake. Saudi Arabia has spent years trying to avoid being dragged back into direct conflict with the Houthis, while its economic transformation depends heavily on regional stability.
"There is no stability, there is no development. There is no stability, there is no prosperity," Al Ajmi told Iran International.
But Houthi attacks on Saudi territory and advances along Yemen’s Red Sea coast are making that restraint increasingly difficult to maintain. The Saudi-led coalition said Houthi missile and drone attacks on Khamis Mushait, Abha and Taif on Monday injured 13 civilians.
Al Ajmi believes some of the Houthis' recent territorial gains could be reversed, particularly if Saudi Arabia decides to deploy its overwhelming advantage in air power. He described Houthi forces operating along the flat Tihamah coastal plain as "sitting ducks."
Saudi Arabia led a military intervention against the Houthis beginning in 2015, with direct hostilities largely subsiding after a UN-brokered truce began in 2022. Years of bombardment failed to eliminate the movement, and Riyadh subsequently spent years trying to avoid being pulled back into a full-scale Yemen war.
The question now is whether the Houthis are pushing that restraint too far.
Houthis risk overplaying their hand
The battlefield in Yemen remains fluid. The Houthis have seized Mokha, Dhubab and Perim Island and expanded their control along Yemen’s Red Sea coast, while Saudi-backed government forces have regrouped and vowed to retake lost territory. That leaves open the question of how durable the Houthis’ gains will prove.
"The Houthis fought the Saudis and the Saudi militias for years. They also have a history of being overextended," Alberto Fernandez, a former senior US diplomat, told Iran International.
Fernandez said the Houthis may have pushed too far.
"I think we could see them lose some of the territory that they've gained," he said.
"They're arrogant. Yes, they're motivated by ideology. And when you're motivated by ideology and you're arrogant, you tend to sometimes overextend," Fernandez said.
But the Houthis are also betting on reluctance from both Saudi Arabia and the United States to become drawn more deeply into the conflict.
Saudi Arabia's attempt to remain outside the wider Iran war has already "certainly backfired on them," Fernandez said.
The uncertainty over how much the kingdom can rely on its allies only complicates its options.
Fernandez described the relationship between Washington and Riyadh as increasingly complicated. The Saudis, he said, felt blindsided by the United States launching the Iran war, while Washington in turn felt unsupported by Riyadh.
That strain has become more visible as Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman sought direct US military action against the Houthis, while Trump declined requests for US strikes and Washington limited its support to intelligence and targeting assistance.
That uncertainty also extends to the Makkah Joint Defense Agreement, signed by Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan on August 7. The pact says an armed attack against any one of the three countries will be regarded as an attack against all.

items.title: مرحله جدید آموزش نظامی به حامیان حکومت در قالب طرح «جان‌فدا»
items.summary: بر اساس پیام‌های رسیده به ایران‌اینترنشنال، شماری از شهروندان در روزهای اخیر بدون ثبت‌نام قبلی، پیامک‌هایی درباره آغاز دوره‌های «آموزش نظامی و امدادی یگان‌های مردمی جان‌فدا» دریافت کرده‌اند.
items.body_text:
بر اساس پیامهای رسیده به ایراناینترنشنال، شماری از شهروندان در روزهای اخیر بدون ثبتنام قبلی، پیامکهایی درباره آغاز دورههای «آموزش نظامی و امدادی یگانهای مردمی جانفدا» دریافت کردهاند.
مخاطبان تاکید کردند آنان و برخی آشنایانشان نهتنها در این سامانه نامنویسی نکردهاند، بلکه از آن «بیزارند».
یکی از شهروندان در پیامی نوشت: «شماره تلفن برخی شهروندان بدون درخواست آنها در این طرح ثبت شده است.»
شماری دیگر نیز با اشاره به همین موضوع، نسبت به درز اطلاعات شهروندان ابراز نگرانی کردند.
این در حالی است که در نسخه فعلی وبسایت رسمی «جانفدا»، گزینه یا سازوکار مشخصی برای لغو عضویت و حذف اطلاعات وجود ندارد.
یکی از مخاطبان با تایید دریافت این پیامک نوشت: «احتمالا جمهوری اسلامی به جانفداهایش کار با اسلحه آموزش میدهد، برای مقابله با مردم.»
مخاطب دیگری هم از این موضوع ابراز نگرانی کرد و گفت: «آموزشهای نظامی به شهروندان عادی در آینده برای استفاده از آنان در موقعیتهای امنیتی یا اعتراضات به کار گرفته خواهد شد، نه برای جنگ.»
بر اساس اطلاعیهای که مخاطبان در اختیار ایراناینترنشنال قرار دادند، همزمان با آغاز این دورهها، هزار «گردان مقاومت ملی» متشکل از ثبتنامکنندگان در طرح جانفدا تشکیل خواهد شد.
همچنین قرار است اعضای این گردانها آموزشهای نظامی و امدادی ببینند تا در صورت وقوع جنگ، امکان اعزام سریع آنان فراهم شود.
سامانه «جانفدا» یک پویش تبلیغاتی و بسیجمحور است که در فروردینماه امسال و همزمان با جنگ میان جمهوری اسلامی و آمریکا راهاندازی شد و از شهروندان میخواست آمادگی خود را برای آنچه «دفاع از ایران» خوانده میشد، اعلام کنند.
رسانهها و مقامهای حکومتی با انتشار آمارهای میلیونی از ثبتنام در این سامانه، تلاش کردند «جانفدا» را نمادی از حمایت گسترده مردمی و آمادگی جامعه برای همراهی با حکومت در شرایط جنگی معرفی کنند.
اواخر تیر شایعهای در شبکههای اجتماعی منتشر شد که میگفت ثبتنامکنندگان پویش «جانفدا» قرار است برای حضور در جبهههای جنگ و عملیات زمینی فراخوانده شوند.
همزمان، پیامهایی درباره «خارجشدن پویش از حالت نمادین» و ارسال پیامک به اعضا منتشر شد.
در پی این خبر، عبارت «لغو عضویت جانفدا» در جستوجوهای فارسی گوگل ترند شد.
تصاویر منتشرشده از دادههای گوگل ترندز نشان میداد میزان جستوجوی این عبارت طی ۲۴ ساعت حدود پنج هزار درصد افزایش یافت و به یکی از ترندهای اصلی تبدیل شد.
روایتهای جدید مخاطبان درباره طرحهای آموزش و سازماندهی حامیان حکومت در حالی به ایراناینترنشنال رسیده که طی هفته گذشته، شماری از شهروندان از بهکارگیری کودکان و نوجوانان در ایستهای بازرسی که بار دیگر در برخی نقاط دایر شدهاند، خبر دادهاند.
استفاده از کودکان و نوجوانان در ایستهای بازرسی و تجمعهای حکومتی و انتشار تصاویری از آموزش کار با اسلحه به آنان در مساجد و پایگاههای بسیج، از جمله اقدامهای تبلیغاتی حکومت در ماههای گذشته بود که واکنشهای گستردهای را برانگیخت.
جمهوری اسلامی همچنین در راستای همین تبلیغات، ویدیوهای آموزش نظامی و کار با اسلحه به کودکان در خیابان را در صداوسیما منتشر کرد.
مخاطبان از حضور افراد زیر سن قانونی در فعالیتهایی با ماهیت نظامی و امنیتی ابراز نگرانی کردند و استفاده از «کودکسربازها» را خلاف قوانین حقوق بشری خواندند.
در پاسخ به نظرسنجی اینستاگرامی ایراناینترنشنال، ۹۷ درصد شرکتکنندگان گفتند شرایط ایران باعث شده تصمیمهای مهم زندگی خود از جمله، ازدواج، فرزندآوری و خرید خانه و خودرو را به تعویق بیندازند.
بیش از ۱۸ هزار نفر در این نظرسنجی آنلاین شرکت کردند و گفتند برنامهریزی بلندمدت زندگی برایشان ممکن نیست.
بررسی کامنتها نشان میدهد ازدواج، فرزندآوری، مسکن، درمان، راهاندازی کسبوکار و مهاجرت، از پرتکرارترین تصمیمهایی بودهاند که به گفته مخاطبان، عقب افتاده یا کنار گذاشته شدهاند.

items.body_text:
اخراج غیرمنتظره دینو تاپمولر از هدایت لانس تنها پس از چهار هفته
به نوشته نشریه اکیپ، باشگاه لانس فرانسه در تصمیمی غیرمنتظره، دینو تاپمولر، سرمربی ۴۵ ساله آلمانی خود را تنها پس از چهار هفته حضور در لیگ یک فرانسه برکنار کرد.
او که تابستان امسال هدایت این تیم را بر عهده گرفته بود، در نخستین بازی رسمی فصل با شکست پاریسنژرمن قهرمان سوپرجام فرانسه شد و یک پیروزی نیز در لیگ قهرمانان به دست آورد؛ اما تساوی مقابل لومان و کسب ۴ امتیاز از چهار بازی، مدیران باشگاه را به تغییر کادر فنی واداشت.
تاپمولر روی نیمکت لانس در دیدار جمعهشب برابر موناکو حضور نخواهد داشت. مدیریت باشگاه تصمیم دارد هدایت تیم را بهطور موقت به یانیک کاوزاک، دستیار تاپمولر، و بلال حمدی بسپارد.
کاوزاک از هفتهها پیش گزینهای جدی برای هدایت لانس بوده است.
•
علیرضا دبیر، رئیس فدراسیون کشتی، از رانت معافیت فدراسیون تحت کنترلش از دریافت گواهی صلاحیت فنی و مالی برای ورود به حوزه معدن دفاع کرد و آن را قانونی دانست.
دبیر گفت: «معدن برای فدراسیون کشتی است و شخصی نیست. اساسنامه فدراسیون کشتی از قبل نوشته شده و یک بندش نوشته فدراسیون کشتی میتواند کار اقتصادی کند. خیلی از دستگاهها کار اقتصادی میکنند. بند اساسنامهشان است و قانون است. میتوانیم ساختوساز هم بکنیم.»
پیشتر، فدراسیون کشتی پس از انتشار گزارش ایراناینترنشنال، با استناد به اساسنامه فدراسیون کشتی، «انجام هرگونه فعالیت اقتصادی، بازرگانی، تبلیغاتی و تولیدی» را حق خود دانست.
شورای عالی معادن در جلسه روز ۲۷ مرداد ۱۴۰۵، برای «جبران بخشی از خسارات وارده به فدراسیون کشتی» در جنگ ۴۰روزه، با حداکثر آرا، به این فدراسیون ورزشی معافیت از دریافت «گواهی صلاحیت فنی و مالی» و مجوز اکتشاف معدنی داده است.
این در حالی است که فتحالله توسلی، نماینده مجلس شورای اسلامی، پیش از این در شبکه اجتماعی ایکس نوشته بود این معافیت با فشار به وزارت صمت به فدراسیون کشتی داده شده است: «یکی از فدراسیونهای ورزشی با فشار به وزارت صنعت و معدن از این وزارت معافیت صلاحیت فنی برای ثبت محدودههای اکتشافی دریافت کرده است! واقعاً در این کشور چه خبر است؛ فدراسیون ورزشی را چه به معدن؟ معدن را چه به فدراسیون و بعد چرا صلاحیت فنی باید معاف شود؟»
«قطعی و لازمالاجراست»
نکته اینکه در نامه وجیهالله جعفری، معاون امور معادن وزیر صمت و دبیر شورای عالی معادن، به مدیران کل صمت در تمام استانها و مناطق آزاد، آمده است که رأی شورای عالی معادن برای دادن معافیت اکتشافات معدنی به فدراسیون کشتی، «قطعی و لازمالاجرا»ست و معاون وزیر از مدیران کل خواسته «رونوشتی از اقدامات بهعملآمده را به دبیرخانه شورای عالی معادن ارسال کنند.»
فدراسیون کشتی که با این مصوبه از اصل تخصص در اکتشاف معدن معاف شده، نداشتن مهندس معدن در ارکان مدیریتی خود را مانعی برای ورود به این حوزه ندانسته و گفته است میتواند توان تخصصی لازم را در مرحله اجرای عملیات معدنی تأمین کند.
با وجود اینکه طبق قوانین اکتشاف معدن در ایران، هر شخصی که منطقهای را اکتشاف کند و به ماده معدنی برسد، وزارت صمت با توجه به صلاحیتهای تخصصی و مالی برای او «گواهی کشف» صادر میکند و به او حق تقدم در بهرهبرداری و استخراج از این معدن را میدهد، اما فدراسیون کشتی چنین رویهای را که نیاز به تخصص دارد، اینگونه توجیه میکند: «این تصمیم نه واگذاری معدن است، نه اعطای حق تقدم نسبت به محدودهای خاص و نه معافیت از اعمال مقررات فنی؛ بلکه ناظر بر تعیین نحوه احراز صلاحیت یک نهاد عمومی دارای ساختار قانونی خاص در چارچوب اختیارات مقرر است.»
ثروت عمومی در دست فدراسیون ورزشی
اصل ۴۵ قانون اساسی، معادن را صراحتاً در شمار انفال و ثروتهای عمومی قرار داده است. معافیت یک فدراسیون ورزشی از احراز صلاحیت فنی و مالی برای ورود به حوزهای غیرتخصصی، در عمل یکی از موانع دسترسی به این ثروت عمومی را برای مدیران آن کنار میزند و زمینه سوءاستفاده از منابع عمومی را فراهم میکند.
نکته اینجاست که با همین توجیه، سپاه پاسداران و دیگر نهادهای نظامی در جمهوری اسلامی مجوز فروش و صادرات نفت گرفتند و در نهایت بخش بزرگی از فروش نفت، بهعنوان ثروت مردم ایران، از اختیار دولت خارج شد.
تیم فوتبال استقلال در نخستین دیدار خود در لیگ نخبگان آسیا، السد قطر را با نتیجه سه بر صفر شکست داد. گلهای استقلال را یاسر آسانی در دقیقه ۹، سعید سحرخیزان در دقیقه ۴۷ روی پاس یاسر آسانی و اسماعیل قلیزاده در دقیقه ۵+۹۰ روی پاس محمدحسین اسلامی به ثمر رساندند.
تیم سهراب بختیاریزاده با این برد و تفاضل گل مثبت ۳، صدرنشین جدول غرب لیگ نخبگان آسیا شد.
استقلال در حالی در برابر السد کلینشیت کرد که تیم قطری، در ۲۲ بازی رسمی گذشته خود، حداقل یک گل به

items.body_text:
در پاسخ به نظرسنجی اینستاگرامی ایراناینترنشنال، ۹۷ درصد شرکتکنندگان گفتند شرایط ایران باعث شده تصمیمهای مهم زندگی خود از جمله، ازدواج، فرزندآوری و خرید خانه و خودرو را به تعویق بیندازند.
بیش از ۱۸ هزار نفر در این نظرسنجی آنلاین شرکت کردند و گفتند برنامهریزی بلندمدت زندگی برایشان ممکن نیست.
بررسی کامنتها نشان میدهد ازدواج، فرزندآوری، مسکن، درمان، راهاندازی کسبوکار و مهاجرت، از پرتکرارترین تصمیمهایی بودهاند که به گفته مخاطبان، عقب افتاده یا کنار گذاشته شدهاند.
از نظر جنسیت، ۶۲ درصد شرکتکنندگان در نظرسنجی را مردان و ۳۸ درصد را زنان تشکیل میدهند.
بیشترین رده سنی پاسخدهندگان با ۳۶.۶ درصد، مربوط به بازه ۲۵ تا ۳۴ سال است. رده سنی ۱۸ تا ۲۴ سال ۱۰.۱ درصد، ۳۵ تا ۴۴ سال ۳۱.۷ درصد و بازه سنی ۴۵ تا ۵۴ سال، ۱۲.۹ درصد از پاسخدهندگان را شامل میشوند.
بررسی هزاران نظر ثبت شده در بخش کامنتهای این پست، نشان میدهد برای بسیاری، تنها یک تصمیم مشخص به تعویق نیفتاده است. شهروندان میگویند امکان برنامهریزی بلندمدت را از دست دادهاند و زندگیشان به تامین نیازهای روزانه، روزمرگی و انتظار برای روشنتر شدن آینده محدود شده است.
عبارتهایی مانند «زندگی کردن را عقب انداختیم»، «فقط تلاش میکنیم زنده بمانیم» و «نمیتوانیم برای آینده تصمیم بگیریم»، بارها در پاسخها تکرار شدهاند.
ازدواج و فرزندآوری
هزینه مسکن، جهیزیه و مراسم، همراه با نبود اطمینان به آینده، از مهمترین موانع ازدواج ذکر شده است.
یک شهروند گفت ۱۵ ماه منتظر فراهم شدن شرایط مالی برای ازدواج مانده، اما فشار و بلاتکلیفی، در نهایت به جدایی او و شریک عاطفیاش منجر شده است.
این روایتها با نتایج یک نظرسنجی دیگر ایراناینترنشنال در دوم شهریور همراستا هستند که ۹۰ درصد از حدود ۱۰۰ هزار شرکتکننده آن گفته بودند در وضعیت فعلی کشور، تمایلی به ازدواج یا فرزندآوری ندارند.
فرزندآوری نیز برای شماری از شهروندان به تصمیمی دشوار یا کنار گذاشته شده، تبدیل شده است.
مردی نوشت خبر بارداری همسرش به جای شادی، نگرانی او را بیشتر کرده است.
مخاطب دیگری گفت پس از ۱۱ سال ازدواج و در ۴۱ سالگی، همچنان از بچهدار شدن میترسد و توان پرداخت هزینه درمان ناباروری را نیز ندارد.
تعویق ازدواج و فرزندآوری در این شرایط، از انتخاب شخصی خارج شده و میتواند نشانه کاهش امید به ثبات و امنیت آینده باشد.
از مسکن و درمان تا خرید مواد غذایی
مسکن و اجاره خانه، از دیگر محورهای پرتکرار در نظرات شهروندان است.
برخی گفتند خرید یا ساخت خانه را متوقف کردهاند و شماری افزایش اجاره را عامل مصرف بخش بزرگی از درآمد خود دانستند.
یک نفر نوشت ناچار شده پولی را که برای خرید خودرو کنار گذاشته بوده، صرف رهن و اجاره خانه کند.
فشار اقتصادی به نیازهای ناچیز روزمره نیز رسیده و کاربران گفتند که بر تصمیمهای کوچکتر هم اثر گذاشته است.
مخاطبان از تعویق تعمیر خودرو، خرید تلفن همراه، لباس، تفریح و حتی مواد غذایی نوشتند.
یکی از آنها تغییر اولویتهای خود را اینگونه خلاصه کرد: «قبلا خانه، بعد ماشین، بعد گوشی، بعد پسانداز، بعد لباس؛ الان گوشت و مرغ.»
بعضی تاکید کردند حتی تصمیمهای کوچکتر مثل خرید لباس، رفتن به باشگاه، رستوران یا سفر هم حذف شده؛ یعنی فشار از پروژههای بزرگ زندگی به روزمرگی رسیده است.
تکرار عبارت «وضعیت بقا» در نظرات مخاطبان نیز نشان میدهد مساله از کاهش قدرت خرید فراتر رفته و مردم احساس میکنند امکان انتخاب و کنترل بر زندگیشان را از دست دادهاند.
درمان هم برای شماری از پاسخدهندگان به تصمیمی تبدیل شده که میتوان آن را تا زمانی نامعلوم، عقب انداخت.
گروهی از مخاطبان، از عقب انداختن درمان دندان، انجام آزمایشهای پزشکی، درمان بیماری و خرید دارو خبر دادند.
کسبوکار، تحصیل و مهاجرت در حالت انتظار
بیثباتی و نگرانی از آینده نیز در بسیاری از پاسخها دیده میشود.
برخی گفتند راهاندازی کسبوکار را به دلیل تورم و احتمال جنگ متوقف کردهاند.
مخاطبی که قصد راهاندازی آموزشگاه نقاشی داشته، نوشت اطرافیان به او توصیه کردهاند فعلا منصرف شود، زیرا هم هزینه ابزار کار افزایش یافته و هم در صورت وقوع دوباره جنگ، ممکن است تقاضا کاهش یابد.
تحصیل و مهاجرت هم از این بلاتکلیفی متاثر شدهاند.
یک مخاطب گفت با وجود دریافت پذیرش دکترا، برنامه مهاجرت تحصیلیاش به دلیل مشکلات اقتصادی و برگزار نشدن آزمون آیلتس، معلق مانده است.
ایراناینترنشنال هشتم شهریور در گزارشی درباره لغو آزمونهای بینالمللی زبان نوشت هزینه مهاجرت، افت ارزش پول ملی و محدودیت آزمونهای زبان، از مهمترین نگرانیهای متقاضیان مهاجرت تحصیلی شدهاند.
پیشتر، در نظرسنجی ۲۱ مرداد ایراناینترنشنال، ۸۳ درصد از حدود ۱۰۰ هزار شرکتکننده گفته بودند در صورت فراهم بودن امکان، از ایران مها

items.title: Ukrainian Olympian Urges US To Bar Russian Athletes From 2028 Games
items.summary: Ukrainian skeleton racer and Olympian Vladyslav Heraskevych is urging US lawmakers and the State Department to deny visas to Russian athletes who seek to compete under the Russian flag at the 2028 Olympic Games in LA, arguing that Moscow has turned sport into an instrument of war propaganda.
items.body_text:
WASHINGTON -- Ukrainian skeleton racer and Olympian Vladyslav Heraskevych is urging US lawmakers and the State Department to deny visas to Russian athletes who seek to compete under the Russian flag at the 2028 Summer Olympic Games in Los Angeles, arguing that Moscow has turned sport into an instrument of war propaganda.
Heraskevych, who is visiting Washington to meet with members of Congress and other US decisionmakers, said the United States has a role to play in preventing the Los Angeles Olympics from becoming a platform for Kremlin messaging.
His appeal comes after the International Olympic Committee (IOC) moved to restore the Russian Olympic Committee's status and lifted recommendations that had restricted Russian participation in international competitions.
“We are living in a real world," Heraskevych told RFE/RL in an interview on September 14. "Competitions are taking place in real countries, in real places.”
He said that while international sports bodies can make recommendations, governments control access to their territory -- giving the US a potential means of preventing Russian athletes from taking part.
Heraskevych is calling on Washington to maintain restrictions that allow eligible Russian athletes to compete only as neutrals, without Russian flags, symbols, or official delegations.
"Our main goal is to show these particular cases, these particular names, and to present that sport is not out of politics," he said.
Russian Sport 'Used In Propaganda'
Heraskevych said policymakers need to abandon what he called the mistaken assumption that sport can be separated from politics. Many people "believe that sport is out of politics," he said. "But Russian sport is being used in propaganda."
He pointed to Russian athletes' participation in political events, support for President Vladimir Putin's ruling political establishment, and activities connected to Russia's war effort against Ukraine.
Heraskevych also cited what he described as Russian athletes' involvement in events linked to Ukrainian children who were forcibly taken to Russia and their participation in military-related activities.
He said the use of sport for political purposes predates Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, pointing to the massive doping scandal surrounding Russian sport and the 2014 Sochi Winter Olympics. "We all remember how Russian security services were involved in this scandal," he said.
Heraskevych said Russia has since expanded its use of sport to promote militarization and normalize the occupation of Ukrainian territory.
He cited Russia's so-called Youth Army movement, which he said is aimed at preparing a new generation for military service, as well as sporting competitions in which Russian organizers present occupied Ukrainian territories as part of Russia.
"These are just a few examples of how Russia uses sport, uses this platform to spread their propaganda, to empower and to make their war machine powerful," he said.
Kateryna Lisunova, a media adviser at the US-based nonprofit Razom for Ukraine, which is supporting Heraskevych's Washington campaign, said the effort is also aimed at warning Americans about how Moscow uses seemingly apolitical institutions.
"It is important to inform American representatives and American people as well as for them to not become a tool in Russian hands in war propaganda," Lisunova told RFE/RL.
She said Russia has used "many good things such as art and sport" to promote and normalize the war and make audiences feel "as if nothing is happening."

items.title: 'Putin Is Watching': US House Panel Advances Russia-Iran Sanctions Bill
items.summary: The US House Rules Committee has advanced legislation imposing tougher sanctions on Russia and Iran, clearing a key procedural hurdle for a possible House vote later this week but exposing deep Democratic concerns over the measure’s expansion of presidential tariff authority.
items.body_text:
WASHINGTON -- The US House Rules Committee has advanced legislation imposing tougher sanctions on Russia and Iran, clearing a key procedural hurdle for a possible House vote later this week but exposing deep Democratic concerns over the measure's expansion of presidential tariff authority.
The committee voted 7-3 late on September 14 to advance a rule setting up debate on the legislation. Debate on the rule is expected to begin around noon local time on September 15. If the rule is approved, the House is expected to consider final passage of the sanctions package on September 16.
The legislation, known as the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, is named for the late Republican senator who championed the measure before his death. The Senate approved the legislation by an overwhelming 86-11 vote in August, giving the House a measure with substantial bipartisan backing in the upper chamber.
The House version was introduced by Republican Representative Michael McCaul of Texas with Democratic Representative Steny Hoyer of Maryland and other bipartisan cosponsors.
But the legislation has faced a more difficult path in the House, where Democrats have objected primarily to provisions that would give President Donald Trump broad new authority to impose tariffs on countries buying Russian energy or helping Moscow evade sanctions.
McCaul: 'Putin Is Watching'
McCaul, a senior Republican voice on foreign policy, urged lawmakers to move quickly.
"Putin is watching," McCaul told the committee, warning that Russia, China, Iran, and North Korea were working together to challenge the United States and its allies.
He argued that the legislation would target the financial networks supporting Russia's war effort, including Russian officials, oligarchs, financial institutions and the so-called shadow fleet used to transport Russian oil.
The bill also extends sanctions on Iran that are due to expire at the end of the year, targeting funding for Iran's energy and weapons sectors. McCaul argued that Russia and Iran could not be treated as separate challenges because of their military cooperation.
The legislation would give Trump authority to impose tariffs of up to 100 percent on major purchasers of Russian oil and natural gas and countries accused of helping Moscow evade energy sanctions.
Democrats say that authority is too broad and could raise prices for American consumers or be used beyond the bill's stated Russia-related purpose.
Representative Gregory Meeks of New York, the top Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, said he strongly supports additional pressure on Russia but opposed the bill in its current form.
Meeks said the president already has extensive authority to impose sanctions on Russia and argued that the legislation would do less to force new sanctions than it would to expand presidential control over tariffs.
"American families will pay the cost of this bill. Vladimir Putin will not," he argued.
Meeks and other Democrats proposed amendments that would have removed the secondary tariff provisions, tightened the president's ability to waive sanctions, clarified that the European Union could not be treated as a single "country" for tariff purposes, and provided additional military financing for Ukraine.
Another Democratic proposal would have identified 10 countries as initially eligible for tariffs of up to 100 percent because of their purchases of Russian oil and gas or their alleged role in sanctions evasion. The list included China, India, Azerbaijan, Turkey, the United Arab Emirates, Hungary, Slovakia, Singapore, Kazakhstan, and Kyrgyzstan.
Meeks also sought to require that sanctions be waived only when doing so was "vital to the national security of the US."
The committee rejected the Democratic amendments.

items.title: Russia, Ukraine Exchange Strikes As NATO Jet Shoots Down Drone In Lithuania
items.summary: Russia and Ukraine exchanged strikes overnight, hitting a gas station and an oil refinery, according to local authorities and monitoring Telegram channels.
items.body_text:
Russia and Ukraine exchanged strikes overnight, hitting gas stations and an oil refinery, respectively, according to local authorities and monitoring Telegram channels.
The attacks on September 14-15 came just hours after US President Donald Trump said Moscow and Kyiv had agreed not to target each other's energy facilities.
Separately, Lithuanian authorities said a NATO fighter jet shot down a drone that entered the country's airspace early on September 15.
In the Ukrainian capital, two gas stations and warehouse facilities were hit on September 15, and one man was hospitalized in serious condition following the attack, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko reported.
Klitschko later said the man injured in the morning attack had died in hospital.
Russia has recently expanded its strikes to gas stations in Kyiv, with Ukrainian authorities saying around 300 such facilities have been hit in recent months, most of them in or near Ukraine’s frontline regions.
Meanwhile, a missile attack on the Russian city of Taganrog, near the Ukrainian border, damaged a warehouse owned by online retailer Ozon, as well as warehouses belonging to agricultural companies, regional Governor Yuri Slyusar said on September 15.
The Russian region of Samara was also targeted by drones overnight, with an industrial facility sustaining damage, according to regional Governor Vyacheslav Fedorishchev, who added that 40 drones had been destroyed during the attack. He did not identify the facility. The region is home to a number of large oil refineries.
Monitoring Telegram channels reported that a fire was visible in the industrial area of the Syzran oil refinery in the Samara region following a drone attack.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed Kyiv's strikes on the Syzran oil refinery and other Russian military targets, calling them retaliation for Moscow's continuous attacks on Ukraine's energy and critical infrastructure.
He also welcomed a decision by the US Treasury on September 14 to target Russia's VTB Bank, saying pressure on Moscow was needed to create the right diplomatic conditions to end the war.
The attacks came after Trump said in a post on Truth Social on September 14 that "Ukraine has agreed not to hit Russian Energy targets. Russia has agreed to do, likewise!"
In comments following Trump's post, Zelenskyy said Kyiv was ready to stop strikes on Russia if Ukraine's allies ensured that Moscow would cease hitting Ukrainian energy facilities, critical infrastructure, and food supply routes.
NATO Jet Downs Drone Over Lithuania
Meanwhile, in Lithuania, a NATO fighter jet shot down a drone early on September 15, the Lithuanian National Crisis Management Center said, after a drone alert was issued earlier in the capital, Vilnius, and the surrounding region.
"Together with our NATO Allies, Lithuania will defend its airspace," Lithuanian President Gitanas Nauseda wrote on X following the incident.
According to Lithuanian public broadcaster LRT, citing preliminary data from the National Crisis Management Centre (NKVC), the drone came from neighboring Belarus and was heading west.
"We refuse to accept our country being turned into a source of danger to Europe," exiled Belarusian opposition leader Svyatlana Tsikhanouskaya wrote in a post on X.
"Lasting security requires a sovereign, democratic Belarus whose territory is never used against its neighbors," she added.
The incident in Lithuania, an EU and NATO member, came after recent Russian drone strikes near the Polish border, with Kyiv warning that Moscow is "knocking on NATO's door."
"Russia's barbaric strikes at the Ukraine-Poland border in Yahodyn are not just a continuation of its attacks on our state borders," Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiha wrote on X on September 13. "This is Putin's terror 'knocking' directly on the doors of the EU and NATO."

items.title: Zelenskyy says Ukraine will pause attacks if Russia spares infrastructure
items.summary: Zelenskyy insists de-escalation depends on US ensuring Russia's genuine readiness to stop war and attacks on Ukraine.
items.body_text:
Zelenskyy says Ukraine will pause attacks if Russia spares infrastructure
Zelenskyy insists de-escalation depends on US ensuring Russia’s genuine readiness to stop war and attacks on Ukraine.
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says Ukraine is ready to halt its attacks on Russian territory if the United States can secure a commitment from Russia to not hit Ukrainian infrastructure.
Zelenskyy’s comments came on Monday after US President Donald Trump claimed that Ukraine and Russia decided to stop targeting each other’s energy sites, without providing details.
Recommended Stories
list of 3 items
- list 1 of 3NATO pledges more Ukraine support after Russia strikes near Poland
- list 2 of 3Why is Trump warning Zelenskyy not to hit Russian diesel refineries?
- list 3 of 3‘Attacks will be fully autonomous’: Russia, Ukraine race towards AI warfare
Trump’s message came a day after he said that rising diesel prices around the world are “mostly caused by the Russia/Ukraine war” and “not Iran”, in a statement on Truth Social.
Zelenskyy said Ukraine’s halting of attacks would be dependent on the US ensuring that Russia is “genuinely ready to stop this war aimed at destroying life, and to do so for real and for the long term”. Only then would Ukraine take “de-escalatory steps”, he added.
Zelenskyy said Ukraine had proposed that its partners secure an agreement with Russia to halt attacks on critical infrastructure, accusing Moscow of targeting food, energy and other basic facilities “that sustain life”.
Russia’s repeated attacks on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure have put a strain on fuel systems necessary for heating and electricity, leading to fears that civilians could face a difficult winter.
“These systems are vulnerable and Russia has been using this vulnerability, leaving thousands of households without electricity or heating for the past three winters,” explained Al Jazeera correspondent Dmitry Medvedenko from Moscow.
Ukraine has in recent months demonstrated its growing long-range strike capability, targeting Russian energy infrastructure far from the front lines.
“Ukraine might start responding in kind by hitting essential energy systems, and surely the Kremlin understands there’s a ticking clock for both sides to come to some kind of consensus for this winter to ensure that their populations will be kept warm and with electricity,” Medvedenko added.
Air attacks continue
The two warring sides continued to exchange air attacks early on Tuesday, with Russian strikes on Kyiv killing one person and wounding seven since the start of the day, Ukraine’s State Emergency Service said.
Another two people were killed in separate Russian attacks in the Ukrainian cities of Sloviansk and Kramatorsk, it said.
Elsewhere, Russian forces shot down 222 Ukrainian drones overnight, Russia’s Ministry of Defence said.
Ukraine attacked an industrial facility in Russia with drones overnight, damaging the site and several residential buildings in the southeastern Samara region, Russian media reported.
About 40 drones were shot down, Russian state news agency TASS reported on Tuesday, citing Regional Governor Vyacheslav Fedorishchev.
Ukrainian media said the targeted industrial facility was an oil refinery.
A “massive” Ukrainian drone attack sparked several fires in the Russian city of Taganrog, regional Governor Yury Slyusar said. He said on Telegram that two apartment buildings and three private homes had been damaged, as well as an educational institution, agricultural warehouses and a site belonging to Russian e-retailer Ozon.
Zelenskyy said on Tuesday that Kyiv’s forces had targeted a drone production facility in the city.
