items.body_text:
Seven former Australia cricket captains have written to the country’‘s foreign minister, Penny Wong, to raise concerns over PTI founder Imran Khan’s incarceration, terming it a matter of “basic humanity”, Cricinfo reported on Tuesday.
Imran, 73, has been imprisoned since 2023 and was sentenced late last year along with his wife to 17 years on corruption charges they both deny.
According to Cricinfo, the signatories of the letter include Allan Border, Greg Chappell, Ian Chappell, Belinda Clark, Kim Hughes, Mark Taylor and Steve Waugh.
In the letter, they said they were writing “not as diplomats or political figures, but as former captains who felt compelled to speak up”.
“The group makes clear it takes no position” on the legal or political case against Imran, describing that as a matter for Pakistan alone, the report said.
Their concern, they wrote, was with the treatment of any person in detention, calling it “a matter of basic humanity, whatever their politics”.
According to the Sydney Morning Herald, a spokesperson for Wong said that Australia “regularly raises” Imran’s case in discussions with Pakistan.
“We continue to encourage authorities to ensure appropriate medical care is available to him,” the spokesperson was quoted as saying.
Last month, 22 international cricketers — including the Chappell brothers, Border, Waugh, Clark and Hughes — had penned an appeal to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, calling for Imran’s medical treatment in line with Supreme Court directives.
On August 18, the Supreme Court directed the government to move Imran to Islamabad’s Shifa International Hospital, a private facility, within two days for examination and treatment by a multidisciplinary medical board. However, it later emerged that Imran was instead taken to the government-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences.
In February, Indian cricket greats Sunil Gavaskar and Kapil Dev had joined a dozen other former international captains, including the Chappell brothers, Border, Waugh, Clark and Hughes, in demanding better prison treatment for Imran, who they called “one of the finest all-rounders” of the game.
Meanwhile, the government has stated that Imran’s imprisonment is “governed by the Pakistan Prison Rules, applicable judicial directions and security arrangements appropriate to a high-profile prisoner”. It has also rejected allegations that he is being subjected to “punitive solitary confinement, cruelty or deprivation”.

Published September 15, 2026
Some cryptic words from Taylor Swift sent Swifties’ into detective mode as they decode each detail meticulously.
After appearing as a rookie detective in Mariska Hargitay’s Law & Order: SVU parody at the 2026 Emmys, the pop star only needed a few seconds to turn it into a full-blown investigation.
The 14-time Grammy winner just said, “Saccharide. Aries. From the vineyard. North or south.” She immediately denied saying anything, a move that did little to stop fans from doing exactly what the sketch had just mocked them for: looking for clues absolutely everywhere.
Within hours, Swifties were dissecting the phrase, the numbers and even the smallest details in the sketch.
One fan interpreted “Aries” as a reference to the zodiac season beginning March 20, while “from the vineyard” was read as FTV, potentially meaning “From the Vault.”
From there, fans connected “north” and “south” to Reputation and Swift’s self-titled debut album, respectively, with one theory declaring: “REP VAULT CONFIRMED.”
In addition to the number 13, fans pointed to a 10:13 detail in the video and floated October 13 as a possible significant date for a potential announcement or surprise.
One theory suggested a debut-related TV announcement could arrive at 8 a.m. on a Tuesday, while another connected references in the sketch to Picture to Burn, Teardrops on My Guitar and the phrase “the answer has been TV this whole time.”
Even the sketch’s jokes became evidence. Fans have been combing through the conspiracy board, song references and dialogue for possible hints about Swift’s next move.
Some are even wondering whether the elaborate setup could be teasing a future plan, a Taylor’s Version project or something connected to the vault.
Interestingly, the entire joke was built around how enthusiastically fans turn ordinary details into elaborate theories.
Taylor, 36, first joked about Swifties searching for clues, then gave them a deliberately strange hint of her own, and then watched the internet do exactly what it was always going to do.

items.title: Inquiry report finds 'systematic, institutional failure' behind Pims deadly fire
items.summary: Police officers move past an ambulance outside an intensive care unit after a fire broke out at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences hospital in Islamabad, August 26, 2026. — Reuters No evidence of arson, oxygen leak as ignition source.Criminal probe recommended into AC...
items.body_text:
Published September 15, 2026
- No evidence of arson, oxygen leak as ignition source.
- Criminal probe recommended into AC maintenance chain.
- Nursery housed 15 newborns in 10-bed unit.
ISLAMABAD: A comprehensive inquiry into the Pims nursery fire that killed 14 newborns has concluded that an electrical fault in the supply cable of air conditioner number two was the most probable cause of ignition, but that the catastrophe resulted from "systematic and institutional failures".
The report, a copy of which is available with Geo News, found that the fire became visible at approximately 6:38am and dense smoke engulfed the nursery within one to two minutes, leaving an "exceptionally narrow rescue window."
The emergency was not reported to the Capital Emergency Service until 6:54am — a 16-minute gap the committee identified as a principal chronological concern, though CES itself responded within minutes of confirmed notification.
The committee established that the fire did not result from arson, multiple ignition points, an external IESCO fault, a pre-fire oxygen leak, or an incubator or warmer.
The most probable point and mechanism of ignition was identified as abnormal localised electrical heating in the AC Unit No 2 supply cable, though the precise electrical defect and responsible duty holder were said to remain to be individualised.
The report found that PIMS and its senior management bore the principal institutional responsibility for failing to convert known fire safety risks, prior warnings and assigned duties into an effective and verified safety system.
15 non-self-evacuating neonates were housed in a stated ten-bed nursery while only two doctors and two nurses were immediately available — a situation the committee described as "a serious operational mismatch."
The nursery did not have a functional automatic smoke detection and fire alarm system or sprinkler protection, leaving human observation and manual communication as the primary means of detection.
The committee found no adequately documented, approved or rehearsed nursery-specific fire and neonatal evacuation system capable of safely evacuating the actual patient load, and said the record did not demonstrate a systematic, periodic and traceable preventive electrical safety regime covering cables, terminations, insulation, earthing, breakers and thermal hotspots.
The report noted that fire and life safety risks at PIMS were known well before the tragedy.
CDA correspondence, Federal Ombudsman observations from 2015, PIMS's own 2024 acknowledgement of ageing fire safety infrastructure and, most significantly, the Nursing Hostel fire of July 6, 2026 — just seven weeks earlier — had all flagged similar deficiencies.
The committee found that prior warnings and the July 2026 fire recommendations had not been converted into a comprehensive, time-bound and independently verified corrective programme before August 26.
"The specific AC 2 defect may not have been foreseeable, but the need for stronger fire preparedness was," the report said.
The committee was clear that frontline personnel who attempted rescue should not be blamed for the institutional failures that preceded the fire.
"The objective record establishes prompt alarm raising, entry, rescue and treatment efforts by frontline personnel and does not support the generalised allegation that doctors, nurses or security staff abandoned the neonates," the report stated.
It added that "responsibility must attach to the duty holder who had the knowledge, authority and opportunity to prevent or mitigate a proved failure, not simply to the individual most visible after the disaster."
While the committee said no named individual was presently found criminally guilty, it recommended focused criminal investigation into possible culpable electrical installation or maintenance failure relating to AC Unit 2, obstruction of mandatory emergency routes, culpable non-action despite specific prior warning, and any proved culpable delay

Published September 15, 2026
Kaley Cuoco was beyond emotional as her fiancé, Tom Pelphrey, won his first Primetime Emmy Award.
As he won the award for Outstanding Supporting Actor in a Drama Series for his role in HBO’s Task, the 44-year-old actor gave a sweet shout-out to his “very pregnant” fiancée in the audience, who immediately burst into tears.
Pelphrey called the Big Bang Theory star “my favourite actor in this room — my love, my best friend, my partner,” telling her, “I love you more than anything, and our family is the own jewel of my life.”
The Ozark alum also gave a sweet shoutout to their 3-year-old daughter, Matilda, and the baby girl they are expecting.
Sharing the moment to her Instagram Stories, Cuoco, 40, joked, “Not sure I’ll ever stop crying!” In the next slide, she wrote, “Will I ever get over this? I don’t think so!”
Following the win, the couple stepped aside to FaceTime Matilda.
Pelphrey and Cuoco welcomed their first daughter in May 2023, less than a year after they started dating. They couple became engaged in 2024 and announced their second pregnancy in June.

items.title: Mir Raza Ali case: MLO Dr Osama levels allegations against Dr Summaiya
items.body_text:
Mir Raza Ali case: MLO Dr Osama levels allegations against Dr Summaiya
- By Nazir Shah -
- Sep 15, 2026
KARACHI: Medico-Legal Officer (MLO) Dr Osama Sheikh, who conducted the first post-mortem examination of late entrepreneur Mir Raza Ali, on Tuesday levelled serious allegations against Karachi Police Surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed, who conducted the second autopsy in the case.
In early August, Dr Summaiya pointed out discrepancies between the first medico-legal report prepared by Dr Osama and the available photographs. Following this, Ali’s body was exhumed at the request of his family and a second post-mortem examination was conducted.
Dr Summaiya told the judicial commission on Monday that she had faced “threats” after raising questions over the findings of the first post-mortem conducted in the murder case of young businessman Mir Raza Ali.
Speaking to ARY News on Tuesday, Dr Osama alleged that Dr Summaiya was trying to implicate him in the case.
“I swear that Dr Summaiya trapped me,” he alleged, adding that she had told him, “If I have trapped you, I will also save you.”
Dr Osama said he wanted to discuss the facts of the case before the commission but felt that the proceedings had shifted away from the central issues.
“I conducted Mir Raza’s first post-mortem. I am the primary evidence,” he said.
He said the facts should be brought before the court, expressing hope that the judge would give him an opportunity to present his position at the next hearing.
Responding to questions about discrepancies between his findings and the second post-mortem, Dr Osama said the issue was not necessarily about whether something was right or wrong, as certain details could sometimes be missed during an examination.
“No person is perfect. That does not mean things have gone wrong,” he said.
Read Also: Mir Raza Ali’s manager tells judicial commission of alleged police pressure
Dr Osama also discussed his experience in examining firearm injuries, saying that he had examined cases involving the same weapon being fired from different distances made different sizes of wounds.
He maintained that the size of an entry wound does not necessarily have to be smaller or larger depending on the location where a bullet strikes.
“I will try to prove the things I have written in my report,” he said, adding that a review of his timeline of events could clarify several aspects of the case.
Dr Osama further said he had arrived prepared to submit an apology but, unfortunately, did not get the opportunity to do so. He added that he had not been prepared during the previous hearing but had come fully prepared this time.

items.title: Rising inflation drives buyers toward second-hand furniture markets
items.body_text:
Rising inflation drives buyers toward second-hand furniture markets
- By Urooj Rizvi -
- Sep 15, 2026
KARACHI: Rising inflation has forced many citizens to switch to purchasing second-hand items, particularly furniture, ARY News reported.
Severe economic pressure has impacted daily kitchen budgets, making the purchase of brand-new, high-end household items an unattainable dream for many.
Constrained by tight budgets, consumers are flocking to used furniture markets to furnish their homes or assemble dowries for their daughters’ marriages.
With new furniture prices far beyond the reach of the average consumer, used furniture markets have become the primary alternative.
Used items are refurbished to near-original condition through repair, polishing, and fresh upholstery, making them fully functional with only minor modifications.
A used furniture vendor noted, “A new furniture set costs as much as Rs. 300,000 to Rs. 400,000, whereas a second-hand set can be bought for just Rs. 150,000.” Vendors added that widespread financial difficulties are compelling more families to seek affordable alternatives in these markets.
Buyers also pointed out that modern, brand-new furniture often lacks durability due to the widespread use of chipboard and plywood instead of solid wood.
Essential items—including sofa sets, beds, and dining tables—are available at half the cost of new items.
Consequently, both lower-middle and middle-class households are turning to pre-owned markets to buy furniture for their homes and as dowry gifts for their daughters and sisters.
For budget-conscious families, the affordability of these markets has proven to be nothing short of a blessing.

items.title: Gold prices today in Pakistan
items.body_text:
Gold prices today in Pakistan
- By Anjum Wahab -
- Sep 15, 2026
KARACHI: Gold prices fell sharply in Pakistan on Tuesday, September 15, in line with a decline in international bullion prices as investors assessed geopolitical developments and changing expectations surrounding US interest rates.
The price of 24-karat gold fell by Rs4,000 per tola to Rs449,336, according to rates issued by the All Pakistan Sarafa Gems and Jewellers Association.
Similarly, the price of 24-karat gold dropped by Rs3,429 per 10 grams to Rs385,233, while 22-karat gold declined by Rs3,143 per 10 grams to Rs353,143.
In the international market, gold prices fell by $40 to $4,268 per ounce, according to the association.
Meanwhile, silver prices remained unchanged in the domestic market. The price of silver stood at Rs6,802 per tola, while 10 grams of silver remained at Rs5,831.
Internationally, silver prices also traded largely flat at $63.23 per ounce, the association said.
Investors continued to monitor geopolitical developments in the Middle East while assessing the latest US inflation data for clues about the Federal Reserve’s interest-rate policy.
Expectations of a US Federal Reserve rate hike this week strengthened following hotter-than-expected inflation data and a rise in oil prices.
The US dollar also strengthened to a more than one-week high, making gold, which is priced in dollars, more expensive for holders of other currencies.
Read Also: Oil climbs as Saudi pipeline outage, fresh attacks heighten supply concerns
“Markets are now fully pricing in a Fed rate hike following last week’s CPI data. At the same time, the renewed rise in oil prices could reinforce inflation concerns and keep the Fed on a hawkish footing,” UBS analyst Giovanni Staunovo said.
US consumer prices accelerated in August, while a key measure of underlying inflation posted its largest increase in four months, according to data released on Friday. The figures reinforced expectations of higher US interest rates.
Although gold is traditionally viewed as a hedge against inflation, higher interest rates tend to reduce the appeal of the non-yielding precious metal because they increase the opportunity cost of holding bullion.
Gold is generally considered a safe-haven asset and tends to attract investors during periods of economic and geopolitical uncertainty. However, expectations of higher interest rates and a stronger dollar can weigh on demand for the precious metal.

items.summary: Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Ministry of Education announced on Tuesday, September 15, 2026, the postponement of the official start of the 2026–2027 academic year to Sunday, October 11, pushing back […] The post Iraq postpones start of 2026–2027 academic year to October 11 appeared first on Iraqi News.
items.body_text:
Iraq postpones start of 2026–2027 academic year to October 11
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Ministry of Education announced on Tuesday, September 15, 2026, the postponement of the official start of the 2026–2027 academic year to Sunday, October 11, pushing back the previously scheduled launch date of September 20.
According to an official statement issued by the Media Office of the Minister of Education and carried by the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Minister Abdul Karim Abtan Al-Jubouri issued the directive to grant administrative and teaching cadres the operational bandwidth needed to conclude second-round examination cycles for non-terminating grades and finalize campus preparations nationwide.
The ministerial directive also incorporated seasonal climate considerations, citing prevailing high temperatures across the country as a primary factor behind the delay to ensure student health and classroom safety.
Ministry officials underscored that the additional three-week window will be utilized to wrap up logistical, technical, and administrative arrangements, enabling local directorates across all governorates to complete physical facility upgrades and coordinate school readiness before millions of pupils and students officially resume classes across Iraq.

items.body_text:
China CAMC Engineering to construct new airport in Iraq
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Governor of Diwaniyah, Abbas al-Zamili, has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the Chinese state-owned firm China CAMC Engineering to develop Diwaniyah International Airport.
The agreement includes the local company al-Balaghi as a joint partner in the project that will be constructed in the capital city of the south-central province of al-Qadisiyyah, located about 181 kilometers (112 miles) south of Baghdad.
The plan includes the construction of a complete civilian and commercial airport, as well as a specialized free trade zone in the province, to stimulate the local economy.
The airport is designed as an aviation hub to boost trade, logistics, and investment in south-central Iraq. It takes advantage of a recent increase in regional aviation traffic and the revenues generated from the growing number of flights.
This agreement expands Baghdad and Beijing’s existing “oil-for-projects” framework and larger infrastructure agreements. It builds on previous aviation initiatives in Iraq, such as the China State Construction Engineering Corporation (CSCEC) project at Nasiriyah International Airport.
The exact cost, capacity, and timeframe for development are expected to be determined in subsequent phases.

items.title: Integrity Chief, French agencies hold talks to recover stolen Iraqi assets
items.summary: Paris (IraqiNews.com) – The head of Iraq’s Federal Commission of Integrity, Mohammad Ali Al-Lami, held high-level discussions in Paris with senior French judicial and anti-corruption authorities on Tuesday, September 15, […] The post Integrity Chief, French agencies hold talks to recover stolen Iraqi assets appeared first on Iraqi News.
items.body_text:
Integrity Chief, French agencies hold talks to recover stolen Iraqi assets
Paris (IraqiNews.com) – The head of Iraq’s Federal Commission of Integrity, Mohammad Ali Al-Lami, held high-level discussions in Paris with senior French judicial and anti-corruption authorities on Tuesday, September 15, 2026, focusing on expanding direct bilateral mechanisms to extradite wanted fugitives and repatriate illicit Iraqi sovereign assets stashed abroad.
The meetings took place alongside the ongoing official government delegation visit to France led by Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi, aligning anti-corruption cooperation with broader diplomatic efforts to deepen Iraqi-French institutional partnerships.
During talks with the leadership of the French Anti-Corruption Agency (AFA), the Asset Recovery and Management Agency (AGRASC), and representatives from the French Ministry of Justice, Al-Lami emphasized that domestic legislative and regulatory oversight alone cannot counter the cross-border architecture of modern financial crime without proactive international cooperation.
He noted that tracking illicit wealth, executing freeze orders, and recovering state assets require streamlined mutual legal assistance requests, calling for direct channels to remove operational bottlenecks and accelerate judicial proceedings against convicted figures evading justice overseas.
Al-Lami stressed that repatriating stolen sovereign capital represents an economic imperative alongside a legal one, asserting that recovered funds will be channeled directly into vital national infrastructure, public service delivery, and sustainable development projects.
He added that restoring illicit assets and enforcing rigorous accountability are indispensable steps to establishing a secure, transparent business ecosystem capable of reassuring and attracting foreign investors. Pointing to Baghdad’s adherence to the United Nations Convention Against Corruption (UNCAC), Al-Lami urged international partners to actively assist Iraq in tracing and returning funds held across foreign financial jurisdictions to the federal treasury.
The session concluded with both sides agreeing to formalize a comprehensive institutional agreement between Iraq’s Federal Commission of Integrity and the French Anti-Corruption Agency.
The prospective framework will focus on sharing French operational expertise in forensic financial investigations, corporate compliance, and risk assessments across both the public and private sectors, while establishing technical training pipelines to build the capacity of Iraqi investigative cadres and deploy advanced asset-tracing technologies.

items.summary: Hong Kong — Last weekend, as the world worried about the possibility of unconstrained artificial intelligence wiping out humanity, the leaders of the United States and China articulated their visions for the era-defining technology. They came from almost opposite sides of the spectrum. Brushing aside the calls from AI scientists and executives from Anthropic, OpenAI and … The post Trump won’t put the brakes on AI because he wants to beat China. How big a threat is Beijing? appeared first on Egyp
items.body_text:
Last weekend, as the world worried about the possibility of unconstrained artificial intelligence wiping out humanity, the leaders of the United States and China articulated their visions for the era-defining technology.
They came from almost opposite sides of the spectrum.
Brushing aside the calls from AI scientists and executives from Anthropic, OpenAI and Google to slow the development, US President Donald Trump said what was most important was keeping the US in the lead against China in the intensifying AI superpower race.
“We’re leading China in AI…and frankly, I want to keep it that way, because whoever wins AI wins,” he said on Saturday.
On Sunday, China’s leader Xi Jinping made his own call for more international cooperation. Countries should “encourage open source, openness, collaboration and sharing,” he said in a speech in India to Global South leaders, in which he reiterated a proposal for a global AI governance pact – although he did not give details on what that framework would look like.
The juxtaposition of Trump and Xi’s messages underscores the lack of consensus and a deep trust deficit between the two superpowers in the high-stakes race to dominate AI.
The US appears to be increasingly weaponizing its dominance in the sector, seeing it as a strategic asset to be protected, and exported to friendly countries, while China, lagging in the race, is proposing a more open model.
AI will loom large at the highly anticipated Trump-Xi summit in two weeks in Washington. At their May meeting in Beijing, the two discussed AI guardrails but produced limited results, and last week the Chinese Ministry of Commerce said the two leaders had agreed to set up an intergovernmental dialogue on AI. But with their broader geopolitical rivalry, experts have low expectations for any meaningful breakthrough.
How big of a threat is China?
Chinese AI has trailed its American competitors for years. That’s partly thanks to US technology controls that limit Chinese companies’ access to advanced AI processors — essential for training increasingly complex AI models.
But last year Chinese AI startup DeepSeek shocked the global industry with a model that approached the performance of leading American systems using what it said were far fewer computing resources.
Since then, Chinese AI labs have iterated faster, with Alibaba, Z.AI, Minimax and most recently Moonshot unveiling similarly capable models that challenge the dominance of American frontier companies like Anthropic and OpenAI.
Alongside the advances of Chinese models, however, came ever louder US accusations of cheating. Washington, as well as OpenAI and Anthropic, have alleged that Chinese companies stole American intellectual property by training their models on the outputs of frontier US models, a process known as distillation in the industry.
Last week, US federal agencies, including the FBI, National Security Agency, and Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, claimed Chinese AI firms are committing “industrial-scale” theft of their American counterparts.
In a lengthy report last week, Anthropic also detailed attempts by bad actors, including alleged Chinese government-affiliated operators, misusing its systems to develop weapons and conduct surveillance on minorities like Uyghurs in Xinjiang.
In one example, Anthropic uncovered sensitive information about Chinese surveillance attempts because queries from a user – believed to be linked with the Chinese military – sent to Moonshot’s Kimi model were rerouted to Claude, exposing Moonshot’s secret attempt to divert user requests to Claude, the report said. Other Chinese firms like DeepSeek also engaged in such a practice, it added.
Beijing has rejected the allegations, while Chinese AI labs have largely stayed silent. Moonshot declined to comment on the report to CNN last week, while DeepSeek did not respond to a request for comment.

items.title: Canada is pursuing a ‘unique alliance’ with the EU as US ties remain fraught. Here’s what we know
items.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney said Canada is pursuing a “unique alliance” with the European Union, a further signal of Ottawa’s efforts to pivot away from the Washington amid a deepening trade war. The notion of Canada joining the 27-member bloc — or at least pursuing closer ties with it — has gained traction within the … The post Canada is pursuing a ‘unique alliance’ with the EU as US ties remain fraught. Here’s what we know appeared first on Egypt Independent.
items.body_text:
Prime Minister Mark Carney said Canada is pursuing a “unique alliance” with the European Union, a further signal of Ottawa’s efforts to pivot away from the Washington amid a deepening trade war.
The notion of Canada joining the 27-member bloc — or at least pursuing closer ties with it — has gained traction within the country in the past two years as Canada has sought to reduce its economic dependence on the US.
A Wall Street Journal report published Saturday detailed how, in the wake of Trump’s tariffs, Carney pushed to bolster ties with the trading bloc, instructing a special envoy to Europe to scope out possibilities “short of full membership in the EU or its common market,” citing people familiar with the matter.
Speaking to reporters Sunday, Carney said Canada is not “looking to become a member of the European Union,” but rather beginning discussions on forming a “unique alliance” with the bloc, with which it already has a far-reaching trade agreement.
“We share the same values, we have the same priorities, and we have very complementary strengths,” said Carney, who is set to deliver a speech to the European Parliament this week.
Here’s what we know about Canada and the EU’s growing ties.
Could Canada feasibly join the EU?
The short answer is no, at least not as a full member.
Canada, a former British colony, shares deep cultural and historical ties to Europe and resembles European models when it comes to its parliamentary democracy, universal health care and social welfare, among other things.
Canada even shares a small land border with Europe, through Denmark on Hans Island, a small landmass off northwest Greenland.
But while Canada would likely satisfy the political, economic and legal standards for joining the bloc, there is one obvious barrier: it is not geographically in Europe.
To get into the EU, a country must follow a strict, multi-stage process called accession, and its candidacy must be unanimously approved by all 27 member states.
There is a lineup of countries waiting to get in, with nine countries currently recognized as candidates for EU membership.
Other European countries, such as Norway and Switzerland, are not formal EU members but partner with the bloc on trade and open borders.
What would a ‘unique alliance’ look like?
According to the Journal, Carney has suggested to European leaders that Canada take on a tailored, highly integrated role as a so-called “associate member” — an idea that at least some leaders in the bloc seem open to, according to officials from both sides.
Among the things European and Canadian officials have discussed, according to the Journal: reducing trade barriers; laying underwater cables linking Europe and Canada; redirecting pipelines to grant Europe access to Canadian gas; building new AI and tech infrastructure; and even granting Canadians the right to live and work in Europe visa-free.
Under these terms, Canada would have a relationship with the EU that is unprecedented for a country outside of Europe. The EU’s ambassador to Canada told the Canadian Press last week the partnership would be unlike anything that currently exists, without giving specifics.
Details about what a potential alliance could look like have yet to be announced publicly. But there are signs that Canada and the EU are growing closer.
Ahead of Carney’s speech Thursday in Strasbourg, France, the European Parliament announced it will open a new antenna office in Ottawa, underlining its commitment to “deepening political dialogue and cooperation with Canada,” according to a news release.
The allies already share a sizable trading relationship, which has grown steadily since large parts of the EU-Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement came into force in 2017.

items.title: How agricultural reclamation village Al-Ray bel-Rash became beset by weapons, drugs and the informal gold trade
items.summary: Violence is no stranger to the residents of Al-Ray bel-Rash The post How agricultural reclamation village Al-Ray bel-Rash became beset by weapons, drugs and the informal gold trade first appeared on Mada Masr.
items.body_text:
How agricultural reclamation village Al-Ray bel-Rash became beset by weapons, drugs and the informal gold trade                    
                Two armored vehicles, a police car and two small open pick-up trucks entered the Al-Ray bel-Rash village in the Edfu district in northern Aswan in the afternoon of September 5, part of a security campaign targeting the home of Abdallah al-Hugairy.
An exchange of fire that would last around two and a half hours was about to begin.
Hugairy has repeatedly been implicated in incidents of gunfire and forcefully stealing cars, motorcycles and tuk tuks from villagers and dahaba (people who work in informal gold mining), according to Ahmed al-Bagga, a farmer from the village. He also says Hugairy is among those accused of killing a villager about two years ago.
Bagga tells Mada Masr that Hugairy fought most of Saturday’s skirmish alone, before jumping from the roof of his house to that of a neighbor, whose livestock, “his source of livelihood,” was hit and killed by a stray bullet in the fray. Bagga says two police personnel were wounded in the uproar: the assistant investigator at the Edfu district, Mohamed Zidan, and a police conscript. News circulating about the incident recorded Zidan’s injury, without mentioning the conscript or further detailing the raid.
Despite all this, Hugairy managed to escape from the village, while security forces raided another house, killed its owner — whom Bagga describes as a drug dealer — and then withdrew from the area.
The next day, Hugairy returned to the village, “as if nothing had happened,” Bagga says.
The eruption of violence at the beginning of the month exposes the recurring pattern that has taken root in Al-Ray bel-Rash. The village sank into deprivation in the 1990s, isolated from essential resources and services. Residents describe how these conditions gave space and air to the flourishing of informal and illicit arms and drug trades.
Occasional security interventions and clashes, increasing over recent years, have done little to break these trades’ entrenchment.
Instead, the volatile dynamic has deepened the isolation of both the village and its residents.
The village, whose name roughly translates to sprinkle irrigation, was established only around six decades ago as part of a state-sponsored agricultural reclamation project. One of its farmers, Shazly, describes it to Mada Masr as still “the most famous village growing tomatoes in the governorate” of Aswan.
So how has the village become a place whose name, for those in the area, is synonymous with drugs and weapons?
***
Al-Ray bel-Rash was established in 1968 as part of an agricultural reclamation project implemented by the Upper Egypt Agricultural Company in Wadi al-Radisiyah.
When the company was liquidated in 1990, the lands it had reclaimed from the desert were broken up and re-apportioned to individual farmers — the company’s former employees — at reduced prices per feddan payable with a low interest rate over a 30-year period, on condition that the employees accept their redundancy from the company and be barred from applying to government jobs in the future.
It’s here that the problems begin. According to an agricultural administration employee speaking to Mada Masr on condition of anonymity, when the Upper Egypt company was active, it cultivated only around 300 of the roughly 1,500 feddans that fall within the village’s official boundaries.
But when the employees became land owners, they needed to make a living from farming and accumulate money to pay off the land’s cost and the interest. So, they sought to cultivate their new plots to the fullest possible extent.
The village was not equipped to host all of this activity.         After days of fierce lobbying in New York, the United States backed away on Thursday from a vote at the United Nations Security Council on a sweeping arms embargo covering all of Sudan.
Washington had spent the preceding hours trying to line up nine votes to pass the resolution while working to keep Russia and China from vetoing it, according to four UN sources, an Arab diplomat, two Sudanese diplomats and a Sudanese former diplomatic advisor who spoke to Mada Masr in the leadup to the vote. But by Thursday, the Americans had concluded that putting the draft as it is to a vote would end with a Russian veto, one of the UN sources told Mada Masr.
The US resolution would replace the current Darfur embargo, which expires on September 12. The proposal brings weapons supplied to all parties to the war, including the Sudanese military, under international restrictions. That would include drones and related technologies, which have come to dominate the fighting.
The Security Council is now expected to vote on a rollover of the existing sanctions for one month, during which the US would try to lobby members and negotiate changes to its proposal on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in late September, a second UN source said.
The diplomatic battle over the embargo is playing out alongside a war that continues to draw in outside powers and take on a broader regional dimension. With states on both sides stepping in to shore up their respective allies, attention has recently shifted to Ethiopia, where an unprecedented arms buildup has been observed at the Ethiopian Asosa base used by the Rapid Support Forces and its allies to operate an increasingly critical front in the Sudanese Blue Nile.
The buildup comes as Ethiopia’s internal conflict is threatening to boil over and its tensions with Eritrea rise, creating a fast-approaching possibility of several conflicts converging along Sudan’s eastern border. That was the backdrop of Transitional Sovereignty Council Chair Abdel Fattah al-Burhan September 4 visit to Asmara, where he met Eritrean President Isaias Afwerki.
An Eritrean security source informed of the talks told Mada Masr that the two leaders discussed how to prevent Sudan’s war from spilling into Eritrea. Asmara wants a clearer picture of how eastern Sudan and the border areas are being used, particularly as the Sudan-Ethiopia border is a point of overlap between Sudan’s war and Ethiopia’s internal conflict.
Neither side was ready, however, to say what it would do if that overlap develops into a broader regional confrontation, despite the meeting being about working out where the other might stand, according to the source.
For now, Sudan and Eritrea have agreed to maintain high-level coordination and information sharing, according to the source and a Sudanese political source.
Within Sudan, the RSF is trying to give its political project a more institutional face and enough weight to avoid being sidelined from diplomacy around the war.
Over five days in Nyala, the capital of the RSF-led parallel government, Tasis’s leadership body agreed to complete and activate the government’s institutions and form a “national military.” What was left unannounced last week though was that RSF Deputy Commander Abdel Rahim Dagalo has been selected to head the unified general command, according to a source close to him and a Tasis official.
The arrangement gives Tasis a clearer division between its political and military leadership. Abdel Rahim would head the military institution while Mohamed Hamdan “Hemedti” Dagalo remains commander of the RSF and heads Tasis’s po

items.title: Consumer, MSME finance providers must adopt OTP verification within two months: FRA
items.summary: Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) Chairperson Islam Azzam has issued a decision requiring companies and entities licensed to provide consumer finance and financing for medium, small, and micro enterprises to implement, within two months, FRA Board of Directors Decision No. 133 of 2026, issued last July. The decision requires finance providers to send customers a one-time […] The post Consumer, MSME finance providers must adopt OTP verification within two months: FRA first appeared on Dailynew
items.body_text:
Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) Chairperson Islam Azzam has issued a decision requiring companies and entities licensed to provide consumer finance and financing for medium, small, and micro enterprises to implement, within two months, FRA Board of Directors Decision No. 133 of 2026, issued last July.
The decision requires finance providers to send customers a one-time password (OTP) when entering into financing agreements and when the financing is used, while maintaining a record of the OTP.
The measure comes as part of the FRA’s efforts to accelerate the implementation of regulatory rules aimed at strengthening procedures for verifying the accuracy of customer data in consumer finance and financing for medium, small, and micro enterprises.
Under the decision, companies and entities providing consumer finance and financing for medium, small, and micro enterprises must complete the technical and regulatory measures necessary to implement the new requirements stipulated in Decision No. 133 of 2026 concerning the sending of OTPs within a maximum period of two months.
The rules require all consumer finance companies, as well as companies, associations, and institutions financing medium, small, and micro enterprises, to send an OTP to customers when entering into financing contracts. The OTP must be sent to the mobile phone number verified for each customer. An OTP must also be sent when customers use the financing, with the finance provider required to maintain a record of the verification code.
Azzam said adding OTPs to the customer identity verification system would contribute to the early detection of harmful practices and manipulation in attempts to obtain financing for consumer or productive purposes.
It would also help combat identity theft and the submission of incorrect personal data, thereby protecting the rights of individuals acting in good faith and preventing adverse effects on their creditworthiness.
Azzam said the regulatory rules established by the FRA for verifying the accuracy of customer data across all non-banking financial activities require companies under the authority’s supervision that conduct their activities using financial technology, as well as fintech-related outsourcing service companies, to verify customer data against national identification records and mobile phone ownership records.
Companies are also required to check whether customers are included on money laundering or asset-disposal restriction lists, pursuant to FRA Board of Directors Decision No. 186 of 2024 and its amendments, most recently Decision No. 133 of 2026, issued last July.

items.body_text:
Yemen’s Houthis captured the Hanish archipelago in the southern Red Sea, strengthening their control of a major maritime shipping route after hundreds of government-allied forces withdrew, government and Houthi officials said on Monday.
The group officially known as Ansar Allah deployed on the islands of Greater and Lesser Hanish, located 160 kilometres north of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, adding to their capture of the nearby mainland port city of Mokha and the island of Perim. Forces of the internationally recognised Yemeni government have been attempting to rally and fight back, but the Houthi gains have seemingly come with little resistance.
More than 80,000 people have been displaced in two weeks of fighting, as the internationally recognised government vows to regroup following the swift advance.
Addressing the developments, US Vice President J.D. Vance told reporters at Joint Base Andrews in Maryland on Thursday that the United States is “concerned” about Houthi movements in the Red Sea.
Vance stated that Washington is “monitoring the situation closely” and is “in continuous contact with Saudi Arabia, the UAE, and other affected countries in the region.”
The U.S. administration is “engaged in talks with the Houthis, and we feel we are in control of this constantly changing situation, and are studying it well to ensure American interests,” Vance added.
The Bab el-Mandeb Strait—located on the opposite side of the Arabian Peninsula from the Strait of Hormuz—is a chokepoint that connects the Indian Ocean to the Red Sea, making it a key waterway for cargo traffic to the Mediterranean Sea. The passage is a key route for oil shipments and has become even more crucial during the Iran war, as the Strait of Hormuz, located at the mouth of the Persian Gulf, remains under U.S. and Iranian blockades.
For more than a month, the Houthis have been striking Saudi oil infrastructure and shipping in the Red Sea, stepping up pressure on global oil prices and boosting Iran’s leverage in its war with the U.S.

items.body_text:
Cairo is seeking to upgrade its relationship with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) to “sectoral dialogue partner” status, as Egyptian diplomacy also focuses on escalating tensions around the Strait of Hormuz, the Red Sea and Yemen, as well as efforts to end the conflict in Sudan.
Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty discussed the proposal with Singapore’s Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Home Affairs Zhullkarnain Abdul Rahim, saying closer institutional ties with ASEAN could help expand cooperation with Southeast Asian countries.
The talks also covered efforts to attract more Singaporean investment and localise priority industries in Egypt, with Abdelatty highlighting the incentives offered by the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZONE).
The two sides reviewed progress in implementing agreements and memoranda of understanding reached during the Singaporean president’s visit to Egypt in September 2025, as the two countries prepare to mark 60 years of diplomatic relations next year.
On Gaza, Abdelatty called for moving to the second phase of US President Donald Trump’s peace plan, the withdrawal of Israeli forces from the enclave, and full and sustained humanitarian access.
He also called for early recovery and reconstruction efforts and for the national committee administering Gaza to be empowered ahead of the Palestinian Authority resuming its responsibilities in Gaza and the West Bank.
In a separate phone call with UAE Foreign Minister Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Abdelatty discussed developments in the Strait of Hormuz and Yemen and their implications for security in the Red Sea and Bab Al-Mandab.
The ministers called for international law and freedom of navigation to be upheld and for diplomatic efforts to be intensified to contain tensions and prevent the conflict from spreading, the Egyptian Foreign Ministry said.
Abdelatty also met with Pekka Haavisto, the UN Secretary-General’s Personal Envoy for Sudan, to discuss efforts to de-escalate and end the conflict in Sudan.
Abdelatty reiterated Egypt’s support for Sudan’s unity, sovereignty, territorial integrity and national institutions, stressing that any political settlement should respect Sudanese ownership of the process while ensuring that humanitarian aid reaches civilians.
Haavisto said the United Nations remained committed to continuing coordination with Egypt in efforts to end the conflict, according to the ministry.

items.title: Fuel Shock in Syria: Protests, Price Hikes and the Struggle to Secure Energy Supplies
items.summary: The central challenge is one of balance: securing enough energy to keep the economy functioning without allowing the price of that security to become unbearable for the population. The post Fuel Shock in Syria: Protests, Price Hikes and the Struggle to Secure Energy Supplies first appeared on The Syrian Observer.
items.body_text:
Protests swept through several Syrian governorates on Sunday after the government raised fuel prices by up to forty per cent, intensifying public anxiety over the cost of living and exposing the deeper structural weaknesses of the country’s energy sector.
Demonstrations were reported in rural Raqqa, Deir ez-Zor and Hasakah, where residents blocked roads, burned tyres and, in some areas, prevented crude-oil tankers from passing. Sections of the M4 highway were disrupted, while minibus drivers in several locations either went on strike or considered raising fares to offset the higher cost of fuel.
Public anger focused on the scale and speed of the increases. Residents argued that the new prices bear little relation to household incomes in an economy still struggling to recover from years of war, sanctions, infrastructure damage and declining purchasing power.
Under the revised schedule, octane-95 petrol rose to 195 new Syrian pounds per litre, octane-90 to 185 pounds and diesel to 175 pounds. Household gas cylinders reached 1,600 pounds, industrial cylinders 2,500 pounds, while a tonne of fuel oil climbed to 52,800 pounds.
The adjustment came only days after an earlier increase, deepening frustration and prompting widespread criticism on social media.
An Energy System Under Strain
Yet behind the price shock lies a broader energy dilemma. Syria remains heavily dependent on imported petroleum products, while domestic refining capacity falls far short of the volume and diversity of fuels required by the market.
According to the Ministry of Energy, approximately 74 per cent of diesel demand, 81 per cent of petrol demand and 96 per cent of household-gas consumption are currently met through imports.
Average diesel demand stands at roughly 11.9 million litres per day. Domestic production supplies about 3.09 million litres, leaving nearly 8.81 million litres to be imported.
Petrol demand averages around 8.1 million litres per day, of which approximately 1.54 million litres are supplied domestically and 6.56 million litres imported. Household gas is even more dependent on external supply, with domestic production covering only about 98,000 litres of daily demand of roughly 2.5 million litres.
This dependence leaves Syria acutely vulnerable to movements in international energy markets, shipping costs and regional instability.
The Ministry of Energy says the latest increases were driven by higher international petroleum prices, tighter supplies of refined products, rising freight and insurance costs, disruption to shipping routes and pressure on domestic refining capacity.
The government also cites the temporary reduction in output from the Banias refinery, which is undergoing comprehensive maintenance and rehabilitation intended to raise its capacity from about 80,000 barrels per day to roughly 130,000 barrels per day.
During the maintenance period, however, Syria must import additional quantities of finished petroleum products, adding further pressure to procurement costs.
The ministry estimates the current cost of securing imported petroleum products and natural gas at around 25.2 million dollars per day, or approximately 755.6 million dollars per month. Officials stress that this figure represents the cost of obtaining imported supplies rather than a direct subsidy or budgetary loss.
Syria does produce crude oil, yet production alone does not resolve the shortage. Current output is estimated at about 100,000 barrels per day, compared with an average of roughly 81,800 barrels per day during the first half of 2026.
The Energy Ministry estimates that the Syrian market requires the equivalent of around 300,000 barrels per day across the full energy mix. This figure does not mean the country requires 300,000 barrels of crude oil alone. items.title: After Eight Months of Torture in Transitional Government Prisons, Journalist Ahmed Polat Transferred to Türkiye
items.summary: Polat and his German colleague, Maria Michelmann, were arrested on January 18 in the city of Raqqa by forces of the transitional government. The post After Eight Months of Torture in Transitional Government Prisons, Journalist Ahmed Polat Transferred to Türkiye first appeared on The Syrian Observer.
items.body_text:
Journalist Ahmed Polat has been transferred to Türkiye after eight months of detention in the prisons of the Syrian transitional government, during which he endured severe torture, deteriorating health, and a prolonged hunger strike, according to his family. They stated that Polat was subjected to brutal mistreatment throughout his imprisonment.
Polat and his German colleague, Maria Michelmann, were arrested on January 18 in the city of Raqqa by forces of the transitional government. For the next eight months, no information emerged regarding Polat’s location or condition. His family told our agency that on September 9, authorities handed him over to Türkiye.
After arriving in Türkiye, Polat informed his relatives that he had been tortured throughout his detention and had refused food for the entire period in protest against the abuse. His family said his health had sharply declined and that he had fallen ill due to the harsh conditions and physical violence he endured. Turkish authorities have since transferred him to Metris Prison in Istanbul.
Polat has worked in media across Rojava and Syria since 2017 and is a member of the Free Media Union. Since 2016, he has reported for the ETHA agency and Ozgur TV, and most recently served as an editor and writer for the “Kurdistana Azad” website, established in 2025.
He was arrested alongside German journalist Maria Michelmann, born in 1989, who has worked as a correspondent in Rojava and in northern and eastern Syria since 2022. Michelmann produced reports for several outlets, including ETHA and Ozgur TV, covering field developments, attacks on towns and cities, and issues related to the Rojava revolution.
Michelmann was transferred from prisons in Aleppo to a facility in Damascus before being released in mid-June. She later returned to Germany following diplomatic efforts by the German Embassy. Polat, however, remained in the transitional government’s prisons until his transfer to Türkiye a few days ago.

items.title: Anti-Corruption Court removes electronic tag from Zelenskyy's former aide Yermak "on medical grounds"
items.summary: Ukraine's Anti-Corruption Court extended Andrii Yermak's procedural obligations but removed his electronic monitoring device citing health concerns.
items.body_text:
Anti-Corruption Court removes electronic tag from Zelenskyy's former aide Yermak "on medical grounds"
The High Anti-Corruption Court has extended the procedural obligations imposed on Andrii Yermak, former head of the President's Office, who is suspected of laundering property obtained through criminal means, while releasing him from wearing an electronic monitoring device "on medical grounds".
Source: press service for High Anti-Corruption Court
Details: A High Anti-Corruption Court investigating judge partially granted a motion by a prosecutor from the Specialised Anti-Corruption Prosecutor's Office and extended the procedural obligations imposed on Yermak for 60 days.
The suspect must:
- appear before a detective, prosecutor or court whenever required
- notify the investigator (detective), prosecutor and court of any change of residence or employment
- not leave the previously designated settlements
- surrender for safekeeping to the relevant state authorities his passport(s) for travelling abroad, diplomatic passports and other documents entitling him to leave and enter Ukraine
- refrain from communicating with persons specified in the investigating judge's ruling (other suspects in the proceedings and witnesses) about the circumstances set out in the notice of suspicion.
Quote: "We would also like to note separately that, according to the assessment of an independent medical specialist, continued use of the electronic monitoring device could pose a threat to the person's life and health. This circumstance was one of the grounds on which the High Anti-Corruption Court refused to extend this procedural obligation."
Background:
- On 28 November 2025, Volodymyr Zelenskyy dismissed Andrii Yermak as head of the President's Office.
- This was preceded by searches at Yermak's office.
- On 11 May 2026, Yermak was served with a notice of suspicion in a case involving the laundering of UAH 460 million (around US$10.5 million) through a high-end construction project outside Kyiv. According to investigators, the funds used for the construction may have originated, among other sources, from corruption schemes at Energoatom.
- During court hearings, it emerged that Yermak had consulted a fortune teller about appointments to state positions. He had her saved in his contacts as "Veronika Feng Shui Office". In particular, he sent her candidates' dates of birth and asked for her advice.
- On 14 May, the High Anti-Corruption Court ordered Yermak to be held in custody, with bail set at UAH 140 million (US$3.18 million).
- After the hearing, Yermak said he had not expected such a decision and did not have the money to pay the bail, but had friends who could help.
- On the morning of 18 May, Yermak was released from the pre-trial detention centre after bail was posted on his behalf.
- On 10 August, a High Anti-Corruption Court investigating judge changed the preventive measure imposed on the former head of the President's Office, expanding restrictions on his movement across several oblasts.

items.title: Russian ambassador accuses Denmark of provoking Russian frigate that fired at Danish helicopter

items.body_text:
Russian ambassador accuses Denmark of provoking Russian frigate that fired at Danish helicopter
Russian Ambassador to Denmark Vladimir Barbin has said that Russia plans to investigate the circumstances of an incident involving a helicopter being fired upon, but accused the Danish military of a "provocation" over its manoeuvres near a Russian frigate.
Source: European Pravda, citing comments by Barbin reported by DR
Quote from Barbin: "Attempts by the Danish side to explain the helicopter's provocative actions towards the Russian frigate as 'routine practice' raise serious concerns about the potential consequences of such recklessness."
Details: The ambassador claimed that this was not the first time the Danish military had "carried out dangerous manoeuvres near Russian naval vessels" and that the Danish helicopter had "behaved provocatively".
Barbin also claimed that Copenhagen had never shown any interest in preventing escalation at sea or strengthening mutual trust.
"Russia's repeated proposals to explore the possibility of an agreement on preventing incidents at sea, which would cover both the sea and the airspace above these waters, have consistently been rejected by the Danish side," the ambassador said.
Meanwhile, the Danish Defence Ministry stressed that the Armed Forces helicopter had entirely legitimate reasons for manoeuvring in the area.
Background:
- Denmark summoned the Russian ambassador after a Russian frigate fired two flares towards a Danish helicopter on 14 September.
- Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen, commenting on the incident, said that Russia had stepped up its hybrid warfare against Europe.

items.body_text:
Kremlin calls energy truce "very good" idea but wants free maritime navigation
Dmitry Peskov, spokesperson for Russian ruler Vladimir Putin, has claimed that the Kremlin considers the introduction of an energy truce with Ukraine a good idea.
Source: Russian Interfax
Quote: "Yes, we saw President Trump's post about an energy truce. In general, we certainly consider this a very good idea, a good initiative. We maintain contact with the Americans. We are always on the side of peaceful solutions."
Details: Peskov added that if such a truce came into effect, Russia would supposedly be able to supply its domestic market with enough oil products because its refineries would operate without disruption. However, he said that when it comes to the global market, "the issue is not production".
Quote: "The issue is unobstructed access for these oil products to global markets. To achieve this, it is necessary to ensure safe commercial navigation and the safe passage of oil tankers.
But in general, we again consider this idea [of an energy truce – ed.] very good, and while being in contact with the Americans, we will continue to communicate with them."
Background:
- On 13 September, US President Donald Trump called on his Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelenskyy to stop strikes on Russian diesel fuel, claiming that such attacks are causing a global shortage.
- On 14 September, Trump said that Ukraine had agreed not to strike Russian energy facilities.
- That evening, Zelenskyy said Ukraine had proposed that its partners "secure an agreement with Russia that would stop the destruction of critical infrastructure".

items.body_text:

The Moscow Times reported this in an article, according to Ukrinform.
"I will not answer you," Peskov said when asked whether Russia would stop attacks on Ukraine's energy infrastructure if Kyiv stopped striking Russian oil refineries.
At the same time, he said that "any call for the Kyiv regime to stop strikes against Russia's civilian economic infrastructure can only be welcomed." He also supported the claim that the Russian ban on petroleum-product exports has a "significant" impact on the global market.
"For now, we see that the situation in the oil markets is generally deteriorating. It is deteriorating rapidly," Peskov emphasized.
Russia has banned diesel fuel exports until January 31, 2027, citing a fuel crisis caused by Ukrainian strikes on oil refineries.

items.title: Russian Casualties in 2026 Top 300,000, Ukraine Says
items.summary: Russia has lost an estimated 301,030 service members killed or wounded since the beginning of 2026, Ukraine’s General Staff said. More than 124,000 of those casualties occurred during June, July and August, while Russia’s estimated personnel losses since the full-scale invasion have reached approximately 1.51 million.
items.body_text:
Russia has lost more than 300,000 service members killed or wounded since the beginning of 2026, Ukraine’s General Staff said on Tuesday, Sept. 15.
According to a statement published by the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, Russian personnel losses since Jan. 1 have reached an estimated 301,030.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
The Ukrainian military compared the figure to the combined personnel of almost 150 motorized rifle regiments, assuming approximately 2,000 service members in each regiment.
“Significant enemy losses are the result of effective combat work by all components of Ukraine’s Defense Forces,” the General Staff said.
The Ukrainian estimates include Russian troops reported killed and permanently wounded. Kyiv Post could not independently verify the figures.
Summer accounts for more than 124,000 casualties
The General Staff said Russian forces suffered their heaviest losses of the year during the three summer months, when an estimated 124,170 troops were killed or wounded.
The monthly figure stood at 39,290 in June, increased to 42,860 in July and remained at 42,020 in August.
During the first 15 days of September, Russia lost another estimated 20,360 service members, according to the Ukrainian military.
An official Ukrainian Defense Ministry update published Tuesday put Russia’s total personnel losses since the beginning of its full-scale invasion on Feb. 24, 2022, at approximately 1.51 million.
The ministry said an estimated 1,400 Russian troops were killed or wounded during the previous 24 hours.
54% of Eastern Germans Say Weapons for Ukraine Are Excessive, Poll Finds
At the meantime, the 42,860 casualties recorded in July represented one of the highest monthly totals since January 2025.
The Ukrainian Defense Ministry said its estimates were based largely on battlefield information, including geolocated drone footage. Ukrainian military units reported intensive drone operations targeting Russian troops, vehicles and supply routes throughout the summer.
Russia does not regularly publish comprehensive figures for its battlefield losses, while casualty estimates from Kyiv, Moscow and independent researchers differ significantly.

items.title: WWII Podcast to Which Putin Should Have Listened
items.summary: Listeners to the UK-based WWII podcast “We have ways of making you talk” can see that Vladimir Putin, the self-avowed student of history, has ironically failed to identify that his disastrous invasion of Ukraine has repeated many of the same missteps that led to the failure of Operation Barbarossa – Hitler’s 1941 invasion of the USSR.
items.body_text:
The twice-weekly UK-based WWII podcast “We Have Ways of Making You Talk” (WHW) has addressed almost every aspect of WWII in more than 1,000 episodes since it began in April 2019. It is hosted by comedian Al Murray, who read modern history at Oxford University, and the professional historian James Holland, the latter of whom has been sanctioned by Russia in response to his published views on the war in Ukraine.
The podcast, which also often includes guest historians and analysts, primarily focuses on the causes of WWII and examines the history, campaigns, personal stories, and the decisions made by the political and military leaders. At the same time, it often draws overt and implied parallels between the lessons from WWII and more modern conflicts including Vietnam, Iraq and Afghanistan.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
This level of analysis is nowhere more apparent than in the eight recent episodes it dedicated to Operation Barbarossa, which draws parallels between Adolf Hitler’s catastrophic miscalculations on the Eastern Front and those made during Russian President Vladimir Putin’s so-called “special military operation” against Ukraine.
Putin frequently equates the Soviet Union’s defeat of Nazi Germany during the “Great Patriotic War” to justify his invasion of Ukraine. The current lack of success in reaching his aims, the podcast argues, is his failure to pay attention to the lessons of Operation Barbarossa combined with the structural inadequacies within both Hitler’s and Russia’s autocratic regimes.
Trump Claims Ukraine, Russia Agreed to Halt Energy Infrastructure Strikes
Battle of Kursk
The WHW podcast draws a number of similarities between the Battle of Kursk in 1943 and Putin’s invasion.
Putin’s current strategy is a giant pincer maneuver around the Donbas salient, just as Hitler attempted to surround the Soviet Kursk salient. The defenders now and then had months to prepare extensive fortifications and knew exactly the direction of attack.
Despite the protests of their military, the dictators insisted on head-on assaults straight into those prepared defenses. Putin, like Hitler, believed that force of numbers would allow them to successfully overrun the defenders. Both drastically underestimated the will and ability of the defenders to stand and fight even against the most formidable of armies.
The war has now reached an effective stalemate – Russia’s armor has been largely neutralized by the use of artillery, anti-tank guided weapons and, most of all, by the development of drone technology, sophistication and tactics.
Underestimating the enemy
WHW argues that both dictators assumed their enemies were inferior in every way and that a rapid political collapse and a swift military victory would follow. For Hitler, this was as much necessity as design: He wanted success before Stalin could mobilize the numerical and industrial advantages he could call on.
They also failed to understand the nature of their opponents’ fierce national pride and the level of resistance this would engender. This was made worse by the brutality of the treatment their forces inflicted on the local population, even those who were potentially sympathetic to the invaders – in WWII, many Ukrainians and Belarusians had no love for the USSR.
Hitler’s indiscriminate brutality encouraged resistance among the civilian population in occupied areas. This has been mirrored by Putin’s forces, which have carried out widespread torture and murder of civilians, blocked humanitarian relief convoys, bombed hospitals, shopping malls, apartment buildings and even the theater in Mariupol marked “children” in Russian and have resulted in uniting Ukrainians against the invader.
Fixation with politics
Both Hitler’s Germany and Putin’s Russia are driven by a political orthodoxy that saw the desire to take and control “real estate.”
In Hitler’s case, this was encapsulated in the philosophy of “Lebensraum,” or living space.

items.title: EXPLAINED: Energy Truce in Ukraine – Third Time’s the Charm?
items.summary: Trump said Monday that Kyiv and Moscow agreed to an energy truce – Kyiv says yes but only if others can guarantee an actual and lasting truce, while Moscow has stayed quiet. Previous attempts suggest that clear terms are needed to impose an actual ceasefire – and only if the parties are willing to.
items.body_text:
US President Donald Trump claimed on Monday that Ukraine and Russia have agreed to an energy truce.
But this isn’t the first time the US has attempted to mediate an energy truce. The one in early 2026 was short-lived, while the most serious attempt yielded a 30-day truce proposal in March 2025.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
That, too, soon fell apart, as everyone interpreted the terms differently. But with Trump concerned about diesel prices – a problem he has pinned on Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries, rather than his own war in Iran – Washington may have a stronger vested interest in seeing it through this time, particularly ahead of November’s mid-term elections.
What’s the latest proposal?
There are no actual terms yet – though Ukraine has floated an energy truce in recent weeks ahead of a difficult winter.
By Trump’s account, on Monday, Kyiv and Moscow both agreed not to strike “energy targets” without further elaboration.
“Ukraine has agreed not to hit Russian Energy targets. Russia has agreed to do so, likewise,” Trump claimed on his Truth Social platform.
President Volodymyr Zelensky issued a statement an hour later, saying Ukraine supports the idea – without saying Kyiv has agreed – before adding that it will only do so in reciprocity, if its allies can guarantee that Russia will not strike Ukrainian energy infrastructure for a prolonged period.
“If our partners are ready to ensure that Russia genuinely refrains from striking our electricity system, other energy facilities, critical infrastructure, and food supply routes, then, of course, we are ready to ensure a corresponding halt to our strikes,” Zelensky wrote.
54% of Eastern Germans Say Weapons for Ukraine Are Excessive, Poll Finds
Russia has not officially said whether it has agreed to the proposal.
What happened in March 2025?
Everyone ostensibly agreed to a 30-day energy truce in March 2025 soon after Trump’s return to office – just not the same version.
These differing interpretations allowed both sides to accuse the other of violations and use them to justify retaliatory strikes, while the lack of a monitoring mechanism also dampened the proposal’s effectiveness.
In short, US officials said Washington had reached separate agreements with Ukraine and Russia to “develop measures for implementing” a ceasefire, but the duration and list of facilities differed for each.
From the Russian side, it listed March 18 as the start date – despite the official talks in Saudi Arabia starting on March 23 – and omitted facilities that Kyiv said were included in its version.
In a statement to the news outlet European Pravda at the time, Ukraine’s Ministry of Energy said Russia’s list did not include its oil and gas production facilities, contrary to Kyiv’s agreement with the US. The exact list of facilities Kyiv presented is unclear.
And violations soon took place – on March 28, Russia struck gas production facilities in Ukraine’s Central Poltava region. The same day, Russia accused Ukraine of firing US-made HIMARS missiles at the Sudzha gas metering station in the Kursk region bordering Ukraine, a claim that Kyiv dismissed as a Russian “false flag.”
In other words, no ceasefire.
Why might Ukraine, Russia want an energy truce?
Ukraine is concerned about a difficult winter, while Russia is facing an unprecedented fuel crisis.
For Ukraine, energy infrastructure – including power stations, substations and gas storage facilities – has been hit hard by Russian attacks in previous winters. Repairs are costly and time-consuming, and with the country facing a budget crunch, any further Russian strikes would put additional pressure on a system already strained by subzero winter temperatures.

items.title: Собянин открыл пешеходный мост на Болотной набережной
items.body_text:
Мэр Москвы Сергей Собянин открыл пешеходный мост на Болотной набережной под Малым Каменным мостом. Об этом сообщает корреспондент агентства городских новостей «Москва».
Новый мост соединил участки Болотной набережной, разделенные улицей Серафимовича. Благодаря этому путь от Болотной площади до кинотеатра «Ударник» и пространства ГЭС-2 сократился почти в два раза.
«Возникла идея, чтобы не ходить через Малый Каменный мост, а пройти под ним пешеходным мостом и соединить Болотную площадь, Болотную набережную и площадь перед "Ударником" и ГЭС-2 в единое пешеходное пространство», — сказал Собянин. Мэр отметил, что новый маршрут позволит продолжить прогулку по Якиманской набережной, в сторону Парка Горького и Воробьевых гор.
Длина моста составляет около 170 метров, ширина — 5,4 метра. По оценке властей, в часы пик им смогут пользоваться более 1,5 тысячи человек в час. Жители Москвы предложили выбрать название для нового сооружения с помощью голосования. Собянин поддержал инициативу и заявил, что опрос проведут на платформе «Активный гражданин».
Открытие моста завершило создание единого пешеходного маршрута по правому берегу Москвы-реки от набережной Тараса Шевченко через Воробьевы горы, Парк Горького и Крымскую набережную до острова Балчуг.
Ранее стало известно о планах строительства пешеходного моста в Москва-Сити, который станет частью прогулочного маршрута вдоль Москвы-реки. Строительство запланировано на 2027 год.

items.title: Врач перечислил появляющиеся задолго до инсульта симптомы
items.body_text:
Нейрохирург Виктор Уго Эспиндола заявил, что задолго до инсульта у человека могут появиться симптомы, которые должны его насторожить. Его слова приводит издание Terra.
Эспиндола объяснил, что за несколько недель и даже месяцев до инсульта у некоторых людей нередко возникает транзиторная ишемическая атака. Обычно она появляется за 48 часов до инсульта. Среди симптомов этого состояния доктор перечислил внезапную слабость, онемение одной стороны тела, асимметрию рта, трудности с речью, проблемы со зрением, головокружение и потерю равновесия.
Все эти признаки обычно исчезают через несколько минут или часов, так как проблемы с кровообращением в головном мозге носят временный характер, но это не значит, что опасность миновала, подчеркнул врач. Изменений при обследовании человека и в его анализах во время транзиторной ишемической атаки тоже не наблюдается, добавил он.
Ранее хирург Александр Умнов перечислил самые частые причины инсульта. Ключевым фактором риска он назвал неконтролируемое артериальное давление.

items.title: В Госдуме призвали не допустить потери контроля человека над ИИ
items.body_text:
Депутат Госдумы Антон Немкин заявил, что при сохранении текущих темпов развития искусственного интеллекта контроль над автономными системами и ИИ-агентами станет одним из ключевых вопросов технологической безопасности, особенно если они получат возможность самостоятельно взаимодействовать с интернетом и цифровыми сервисами. В беседе с RT парламентарий подчеркнул, что правильный ответ на эти вызовы не в том, чтобы остановить или искусственно замедлить развитие технологии.
«Гораздо важнее научиться управлять этой технологией: понимать ее возможности и ограничения, устанавливать зоны ответственности и не допускать ситуаций, когда человек фактически теряет контроль над системой», — заявил Немкин.
По его словам, технологический прогресс все равно продолжится, и если одни страны откажутся от развития ИИ, другие этого не сделают. Именно поэтому регулирование становится принципиальным вопросом: с 1 сентября в России уже вступили в силу положения, формирующие базовые правила в сфере ИИ, а следующий этап — развитие этих механизмов с учетом скорости появления новых моделей и агентов.
Отдельной задачей депутат назвал технологический суверенитет, отметив, что контролировать риски ИИ невозможно, если критически важные технологии, вычислительные мощности и ключевые решения находятся за пределами российской юрисдикции. Он подчеркнул необходимость собственных моделей, инфраструктуры и специалистов, не исключая международного взаимодействия и обмена компетенциями.
Ранее генеральный директор компании OpenAI (разработчик ChatGPT) Сэм Альтман согласился, что риск вымирания человечества из-за ИИ достаточно серьезен, и компаниями, занимающимся ИИ, а также правительствам нужно показывать, что это недопустимо.

items.title: NYT: встречу по Ормузскому проливу перенесли из-за разногласий между Саудовской Аравией и Ираном // NYT узнала причину переноса встречи стран Персидского залива с Ираном
items.summary: Встречу представителей Ирана с партнерами из стран Персидского залива по Ормузскому проливу пришлось отложить из-за новых предложений Саудовской Аравии. С частью из них иранская сторона не согласилась, с другими -- пообещала ознакомиться, пишет The New York Times (NYT) со ссылкой на источники.
items.body_text:
NYT: встречу по Ормузскому проливу перенесли из-за разногласий между Саудовской Аравией и Ираном
NYT узнала причину переноса встречи стран Персидского залива с Ираном
Встречу представителей Ирана с партнерами из стран Персидского залива по Ормузскому проливу пришлось отложить из-за новых предложений Саудовской Аравии. С частью из них иранская сторона не согласилась, с другими — пообещала ознакомиться, пишет The New York Times (NYT) со ссылкой на источники.
Высокопоставленный чиновник из стран Персидского залива уточнил NYT, что Саудовская Аравия и Иран зашли в тупик при обсуждении ситуации вокруг Ормузского пролива. По его словам, Эр-Рияд представил несколько поправок, одна из которых противоречила утверждениям Тегерана о том, что Ормузский пролив не входит в число международных вод.
О новых предложениях Саудовской Аравии по Ормузскому проливу накануне сообщал корреспондент Axios, однако об их влиянии на проведение переговоров он не говорил.
Встреча глав МИД стран Персидского залива и Ирана была запланирована на 14 сентября. Стороны должны были обсудить проект омано-иранского соглашения по урегулированию судоходства в Ормузском проливе. Позднее министр иностранных дел Омана Бадр аль-Бусаиди объявил о переносе переговоров для «достижения консенсуса».
