items.title: Trump complains about Google's €13bn data centre, development plans in Finland
items.summary: According to Trump, tech firms are subject to too much regulation in the US.
items.body_text:
US President Donald Trump has voiced displeasure over Google's recently announced data centre plans in Finland.
In a post on his subscription-based social media site Truth Social on Monday, Trump wrote:
"Google has recently stated that they want to build a massive Plant in Finland, all because they are finding permitting too difficult in the United States. I am not happy about this, and want them to change their thinking."
According to Trump, technology firms are subject to too much regulation in the US, a situation that he claims only benefits China.
Last week, Google announced plans to invest 13 billion euros in data centres and other operations in Finland over the next two years—its largest European investment to date.
While some officials say Google's plans will bring thousands of jobs and economic growth to Finland, some experts have cautioned that long-term employment may be limited due to automation and raise concerns about environmental impact.

items.title: Mieli Mental Health Finland cuts jobs as government reduces funding
items.summary: Approximately 160 people work at the NGO.
items.body_text:
Mieli, Mental Health Finland, reported that it has concluded redundancy talks resulting in the cut of 13 positions.
The negotiations and job cut plans were announced last month, when the NGO said that there were up to 20 jobs at risk.
According to Mieli, steep and rapid government cuts to state funding for social and healthcare NGOs forced them to scale back their operations.
In addition to the confirmed 13 redundancies, it said four employees' working hours will be reduced, four positions will remain vacant due to retirement or other reasons, and five employees' job descriptions will change significantly.
The reductions affect a total of 21 positions. Altogether, approximately 160 people work at the organisation.
According to Mieli, its savings measures target units that promote mental health and prevent problems in people's lives.
The group's low-threshold services have proven popular. Last year, its crisis helpline handled a record number of calls, more than 110,000.
"The decisions have been difficult but necessary in this funding situation," Sari Aalto-Matturi, Mieli's executive director, said in the statement.
The funding changes were announced last spring by Social Affairs and Health Minister Wille Rydman (Finns).

items.title: Sjamsudin Noor Air Base serves as Virgo evacuation point
items.summary: Sjamsudin Noor Air Base in Banjarbaru, South Kalimantan, served as an air evacuation point on Tuesday for victims of ...
items.body_text:
"Four dead victims were evacuated today from a vessel near the accident site and flown to Sjamsudin Noor Air Base," Air Base Commander Col. Hilman L.P. Ambarita said in Banjarbaru.
The four body bags arrived at the air base in separate helicopter flights.
Basarnas' Dauphin HR 3601 helicopter was the first to land at about 11:25 a.m. local time, carrying two body bags.
About 30 minutes later, a police helicopter arrived at 11:54 a.m., carrying two more body bags.
The four victims had been aboard the tugboat KM TB TCB, which was being used as a support vessel near the Virgo Transport 8 accident site.
Upon arrival at Sjamsudin Noor Air Base, the victims were quickly and systematically transferred from the helicopters.
The four body bags were transferred to ambulances and taken to Bhayangkara Hospital in Banjarmasin.
At the hospital, police DVI teams will examine the bodies and conduct identification procedures to confirm each victim's identity.
Ambarita said air evacuation efforts on the third day of the search-and-rescue operation focused on transporting dead victims from the support vessel to medical facilities ashore.
Each victim arriving at Sjamsudin Noor Air Base immediately received initial medical attention before being handed over to relevant authorities for identification and further handling.
The support was part of Sjamsudin Noor Air Base's role in the search-and-rescue operation for the Virgo Transport 8 accident.
"Besides supporting air operations, Sjamsudin Noor Air Base is an important point for receiving and evacuating victims found in the Java Sea," he said.

items.title: Indonesia targets 5,000 fishermen villages to boost coastal economy
items.summary: Coordinating Minister for Food Zulkifli Hasan said the government is accelerating the development of 5,000 Red and ...
items.body_text:
Jakarta (ANTARA) - Coordinating Minister for Food Zulkifli Hasan said the government is accelerating the development of 5,000 Red and White Fishermen's Villages (KNMP) through the end of 2029 to strengthen fishermen's bargaining power and improve their welfare.
He said the KNMP initiative aims to strengthen the coastal economy by providing facilities across the fishing value chain, from fishing operations and catch storage to fish processing and marketing.
"We must accelerate equality, prosperity, and progress in this sector. Therefore, priority programs are being fast-tracked, including the construction of 5,000 fishing villages by the end of 2029," Hasan remarked on Tuesday.
He assessed that the lack of supporting facilities weakens fishermen's bargaining power, forcing them to sell their catch immediately before its quality deteriorates. Through the KNMP program, the government aims to strengthen the fishing business ecosystem by integrating fishing activities with facilities for storage, processing, and marketing.
The government also aims to ensure that fishermen are not forced to sell their catch at low prices due to limited storage capacity, while expanding their access to wider markets.
Hasan said the KNMP sites would be equipped with facilities such as fish auction sites, boat access points, cold storage warehouses, workshops, ice plants, and dedicated fuel stations for fishermen (SPBN).
In addition to fisheries infrastructure, he said institutional strengthening through cooperatives is also being prioritized to expand market access and enable fishermen to sell their catch to different parts of Indonesia.
According to Hasan, the government aims to raise the Fishermen's Exchange Rate (NTN) to 120 by 2027 as part of efforts to improve the welfare of coastal communities. He compared fishermen with farmers, whose exchange rate has reached around 129, stressing the need to increase support for the fisheries sector.
Statistics Indonesia (BPS) previously recorded the national Farmers' Exchange Rate (NTP) at 129.19 in August 2026, up 1.05 percent from the previous month.
Meanwhile, the NTN stood at 109.04, increasing 0.50 percent from 108.49 in July 2026.
BPS noted that the increase in the NTN was primarily driven by commodities such as mackerel tuna, Indian mackerel, marine shrimp, and anchovies, which raised the price index of goods sold by fishermen.
The Ministry of Marine Affairs and Fisheries (KKP) previously constructed 100 KNMPs in 2025 and plans to develop 1,269 locations in 2026 with a budget of approximately Rp10 trillion (US$551 million), as part of the government's target to establish 5,000 fishermen's villages by the end of 2029.
One KNMP in Sorue Jaya, Konawe District, Southeast Sulawesi, shipped eight tons of export-quality fish to other regions in August 2026 while still in the trial phase. The village was supported by cold storage facilities, an ice factory, and a jetty.
Hasan believes that providing supporting facilities and expanding market access are key to strengthening the economic position of coastal communities and improving fishermen's welfare.

items.title: KM Virgo Transport 8 sank in less than five minutes, survivor says
items.summary: A crew member of the KM Virgo Transport 8 said the vessel suddenly listed and sank within five minutes after the ...
items.body_text:
It sank very quickly, in less than five minutes,
Akmal said he noticed no warning signs before the vessel began listing, such as shaking or the sound of water entering the ship.
"I was sleeping. When I woke up, the ship was already listing. I ran to my room, grabbed a life jacket and jumped into the sea," Akmal said after being evacuated on Tuesday.
Akmal was among 22 survivors evacuated Tuesday by a Rigid Buoyancy Boat (RBB) from Banjarmasin Naval Base after being transferred from KRI Nala at the scene.
They had been transferred between several vessels since being rescued at around 10 a.m. local time on Sunday, several hours after the accident occurred at around 1 a.m., he said.
Akmal said the ship had been operating normally before he fell asleep, so the listing happened suddenly after he woke, leaving him little time to do anything beyond grabbing a life jacket.
"It sank very quickly, in less than five minutes," he said.
Akmal said he heard an alarm after reaching a safe distance from the ship, which had already capsized, prompting him to move farther away.
"When the ship began to capsize, I saw many people jumping into the sea to save themselves. They were still alive when they entered the water," he said.
Akmal said he was in the rear section when the accident began, far from the bridge, and therefore did not know what had happened at the front of the vessel before it began listing.
He said he was unaware of forecasts for waves reaching two to three meters before departure because he simply followed orders to sail as scheduled.
Akmal, who had worked aboard the KM Virgo Transport 8 for about three months, said he had never experienced a similar incident on the vessel.
As of 9 a.m. local time on Tuesday, the National Search and Rescue Agency (Basarnas) said 114 people had been found, including 108 survivors and six dead. Another 129 people remained missing from the 243 people aboard.
Of the 114 people found, 110 had reached Banjarmasin, including 108 survivors and two deceased victims. Four other deceased victims were being evacuated by air to Syamsudin Noor Air Base for further medical handling.
The Virgo Transport 8, carrying 243 people, lost contact in the Masalembo waters of the Java Sea at around 2 a.m. local time on Sunday, September 13, while sailing from Surabaya to Banjarmasin.

items.title: Remulla says Roque asylum bid denied; Roque disputes claim
items.summary: Two contradicting claims, yet no proof bared just yet.
items.body_text:
Remulla says Roque asylum bid denied; Roque disputes claim
MANILA, Philippines — Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla on Tuesday claimed that former presidential spokesperson Harry Roque's asylum bid in Austria had been denied, a claim Roque later disputed.
Remulla made the statement during a press conference on Tuesday, September 15, adding that authorities would move against Roque once an Interpol Red Notice is issued.
"By the way, na-deny 'yung asylum ni Harry Roque," Remulla said. "Kapag may Red Notice na, kukunin ko siya."
By the way, Harry Roque's asylum bid was denied... I'll get him once there is a Red Notice.)
Remulla did not disclose further details about the purported denial. Philstar.com has also reached out to the Department of Justice for more information but has yet to receive a response.
Roque, who faces qualified human trafficking charges in connection with the raided Lucky South 99 POGO hub in Porac, Pampanga, has been staying in Austria while seeking asylum.
An Angeles City court issued a warrant for his arrest in May 2025 over the non-bailable trafficking charges.
Roque left the Philippines without a recorded departure in Bureau of Immigration records after authorities began looking for him in 2024.
The Department of Justice had earlier issued an immigration lookout bulletin against him and several others in August 2024 in connection with the investigation into the Porac POGO hub.
Aside from the trafficking case, Roque also faces a tax evasion complaint filed by the Bureau of Internal Revenue before the DOJ.
In an interview with One News' "Storycon," Roque denied Remulla's claim, calling it "fake news."
Roque said his asylum application had already been submitted for resolution and that he was still awaiting a decision from Austrian authorities.
"The truth of the matter is it's been submitted and we continue to await for the decision of the asylum office," Roque said.

items.title: Palace: Roque’s asylum bid, persecution claims lack basis
items.summary: Following Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla's announcement that Harry Roque's asylum bid in Europe has been denied, Malacañang said the former spokesperson's political persecution claims were baseless.
items.body_text:
Palace: Roque’s asylum bid, persecution claims lack basis
MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang said on Tuesday, September 15, that the asylum request and political persecution claims of former presidential spokesperson Harry Roque lacked basis as he continues to face charges in the Philippines.
According to Palace Press Officer Claire Castro, during a press briefing, aside from qualified human trafficking complaints, Roque also faces accusations of land grabbing and tax evasion.
“Ang paniniwala ng PCO (Presidential Communications Office) ay wala pong batayan ang ginawang request ni Harry Roque na sinasabing political persecution lang ang ginagawa sa kanya. Maliwanag naman po ang mga kaso, hindi lang qualified human trafficking,” Castro said.
(The PCO believes that Harry Roque’s request claiming he’s experiencing political persecution has no basis. The cases are clear, and they involve not only qualified human trafficking.)
The Palace’s comment came after Department of the Interior and Local Government Secretary Jonvic Remulla said in a separate press briefing earlier Tuesday that Roque’s asylum request had been denied.
Remulla previously said Roque was applying for asylum in Austria, citing political persecution.
In the Philippines, Roque faces non-bailable qualified human trafficking charges filed by the Department of Justice over his alleged active participation in the operations of Lucky South 99, the illegal Philippine offshore gaming operator (POGO) hub in Pampanga, which was raided in 2024.
An arrest warrant was issued by a Pampanga court against Roque and his co-accused in May 2025 for the qualified human trafficking case.
Meanwhile, in March this year, a group of farmers from Bataan filed land-grabbing complaints against Roque for allegedly transferring land titles, which were supposed to be distributed to 100 farmers, to a private corporation connected to a POGO firm.
The corporation's listed address supposedly pointed to Roque’s office.
The Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) also filed a tax evasion case against Roque and his wife in April this year for allegedly failing to pay P3.35 million in taxes connected to transactions involving Biancham Holdings and Trading Inc.
Roque denied all accusations, saying these are all part of the continuous political attacks against him.
He also dismissed Remulla’s claim that his asylum request had been denied, calling it “fake news.”
Roque, who served as the Palace spokesperson under then-President Rodrigo Duterte, left the Philippines in 2024.

items.title: DOJ summons Robin Padilla, 6 others over Bato Dela Rosa escape
items.summary: The Department of Justice has issued a subpoena against Sen. Robin Padilla and six others over complaints of obstruction of justice.
items.body_text:
DOJ summons Robin Padilla, 6 others over Bato Dela Rosa escape
MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Justice (DOJ) has issued a subpoena against Sen. Robin Padilla and six others over complaints of obstruction of justice.
According to the summons, Padilla is required to appear before the DOJ on September 25 and October 9.
The summons were served on the lawmaker and co-accused Lt. Col. Jean Alla Yasin Robles on Tuesday afternoon, according to DOJ Spokesperson Polo Martinez.
The complaints are over his alleged assistance in the escape of Sen. Bato Dela Rosa on May 14, following the shooting incident at the Senate.
It could be recalled that Dela Rosa hitched a ride in Padilla’s SUV on May 14 before disappearing from law enforcement’s radar. Padilla also admitted that he gave Dela Rosa a ride to help him escape.
The DOJ complaint was filed by the Philippine National Police Criminal Investigation and Detection Group on May 28.
A separate complaint of obstruction of justice was also filed before the Office of the Ombudsman against Padilla.
The obstruction complaint against Padilla at the Ombudsman was filed by civic group Tindig Pilipinas on July 4.
In a Facebook post, Padilla said: "A subpoena has arrived."
Dela Rosa, who is wanted by the International Criminal Court, is currently at large due to alleged crimes against humanity.

items.title: Asia's clean-air leader becomes 'unhealthy' for first time since 2019
items.summary: Singapore, renowned for its clean air and strict environmental standards, saw air quality deteriorate sharply on Tuesday, with all five regions recording unhealthy levels for the first time since September 2019.
items.body_text:
At 6 a.m., the 24-hour Pollutant Standards Index (PSI) in the central region stood at 154, the highest among the five. The eastern and western regions both recorded 128, while they were 111 and 104 in the south and north, The Straits Times reported.
By 9 a.m., the PSI readings had eased slightly but remained in the unhealthy range.
In Singapore, 0 to 50 is considered good, 51 to 100 is moderate, and 101 to 200 is unhealthy. And then there are "very unhealthy" and "hazardous" classifications.
The city state has long been regarded as having one of the cleanest air in Asia. According to IQAir's 2025 data, it ranked 4th in the region, behind only the Maldives, Japan, and Cyprus, with an average PM2.5 concentration of 11.9 µg/cu.m.
But that reputation took a hit on Tuesday morning, as haze from wildfires in Indonesia blanketed the country.
The National Environment Agency (NEA) said on Monday in its daily haze advisory that moderate to dense smoke plumes from fires in Kalimantan, Indonesia, had drifted towards Singapore as prevailing winds shifted, according to Channel NewsAsia.
Smoke haze was also observed drifting from southern Sumatra.
"Dry conditions are forecast over Singapore and the surrounding region in the coming days," the NEA said, warning that prevailing winds were expected to continue blowing from the southeast, putting Singapore at risk of further haze."
The 24-hour PSI first entered the unhealthy range on Sept. 4, prompting the NEA to begin issuing daily advisories.
By 9 a.m. Tuesday, PM2.5 readings across the island had returned to safe levels.
The NEA advised the public to reduce outdoor activities when the 24-hour PSI is at unhealthy levels.
items.normalised_title: asias clean air leader becomes unhealthy for first time since 2019

items.body_text:
SMRT Trains president Lam Sheau Kai told CNA the smoke was seen at about 11:40 a.m. at the elevated North-South Line station, and that preliminary checks suggested a faulty brake.
All commuters were guided off the train as a safety precaution before it was withdrawn to the depot for further checks, Lam said.
No one needed medical assistance, and train services along the line continued to run normally. SMRT did not say how many passengers were on board.
A video posted to Instagram by the account sgfollowsall showed the platform crowded with commuters, some covering their noses as smoke filled the area, The Straits Times reported.
SMRT staff could be seen speaking into walkie-talkies while observing the empty, stationary train on the Jurong East-bound side, the newspaper said.
A train emitted smoke from its undercarriage at Sembawang station on the same line on April 13, Mothership reported, an incident Lam attributed at the time to a brake that had remained engaged and could not be released. Passengers were taken off that train and it was pulled from service.
Land Transport Authority figures published on July 17 show North-South Line trains traveled an average of 1.98 million km between delays longer than five minutes in the 12 months to June 2026, against the authority's benchmark of 1 million km.
The line recorded no delays exceeding 30 minutes in any month of that period.

items.title: Foreigners arrested after failing to steal $7,700 in gold in central Vietnam
items.summary: A foreign man and woman were arrested approximately an hour after stealing three gold bracelets worth VND208 million (US$7,700) from a shop owner in Dak Lak Province.
items.body_text:
The suspects distracted the owner to take the jewelry before fleeing in a car with two accomplices.
According to police, the pair visited the Tien Vien gold shop in the central Vietnam's province around 7 a.m. on Sept. 15. The shop had just opened for the day and was empty of customers.
The male suspect engaged the shop owner in conversation, repeatedly asking questions to serve as a distraction. During this time, the female suspect discreetly approached a gold cabinet, unlocked it using a key that had been left in the lock, and removed the three bracelets.
When the owner realized what was happening and shouted for help, the woman dropped the gold beneath the cabinet.
The pair then fled to a white getaway car parked across the street, where two other foreign nationals were waiting. The driver immediately sped away.
Following an emergency alarm from the shop, local police coordinated with provincial traffic police and requested assistance from the Xuan Loc Commune police to aid in the pursuit.
At approximately 8 a.m., authorities apprehended the two primary suspects and their accomplices along National Highway 1D, about 40 kilometers from the crime scene.
Police are taking statements from the four individuals and have not yet released their identities.

items.title: Use of banned ‘red meat’ chemicals in cattle uncovered
items.summary: Thai authorities have arrested a chemical supplier after finding salbutamol, a beta agonist used illegally as a “red meat” enhancer, in nearly 1,000 cattle in an eight-month investigation spanning five provinces.
items.body_text:
Thai authorities have arrested a chemical supplier after finding salbutamol, a beta agonist used illegally as a “red meat” enhancer, in nearly 1,000 cattle in an eight-month investigation spanning five provinces.
Police and livestock officials seized animal feed, raw materials and production equipment worth 32 million baht and uncovered financial transactions of 80 million baht linked to the supplier, Pol Lt Gen Natthasak Chaowanasai, commissioner of the Central Investigation Bureau (CIB), said during a media briefing on Tuesday.
Beta-agonists such as salbutamol pose a potential threat to human health because they can pass from animal feed to cattle and remain as residues in meat.
The substances are used legally in products to treat breathing problems in humans but are also used illegally to increase muscle mass and reduce fat in cattle.
Consumer protection police and officials from the Department of Livestock Development launched their investigation in February, tracing the supply chain from markets and cattle farms to animal-feed production facilities and the original suppliers of the chemicals.
Authorities searched 16 locations in Pathum Thani, Saraburi, Suphan Buri, Kanchanaburi and Phetchaburi provinces and tested 967 cattle, said Pol Lt Gen Natthasak.
Tests detected salbutamol residues in cattle urine and beef. Officials seized or impounded animal feed, raw materials, premixes and production equipment worth a combined 32.4 million baht.
A further investigation found 80.3 million baht in transactions flowing into and out of accounts linked to the supplier of the chemicals used in the process.
Pol Maj Gen Kongkrit Lertsithikul, commander of the Consumer Protection Police Division (CPPD), said the operation began with inspections at markets and meat outlets. Samples were collected and tested for prohibited residues.
When the banned substance was detected, investigators traced the meat back to slaughterhouses and cattle farms before expanding their probe to animal feed and related production processes.
The substance was found in meat, animal feed and feed-production equipment and in cattle at farms suspected of using adulterated feed. The evidence was seized and the investigation expanded.
Discussing the results of the eight-month investigation into banned chemical use in animal feed, from left: Pol Maj Gen Kongkrit Lertsithikul, commander of the Consumer Protection Police Division (CPPD); Pol Lt Gen Natthasak Chaowanasai, commissioner of the Central Investigation Bureau (CIB); Sorawut Nueangchamnong, secretary to the minister of agriculture and cooperatives; and Somchuan Rattanamangkalarnon, director-general of the Department of Livestock Development. (Photo supplied/Wassayos Ngamkham)
Pol Maj Gen Kongkrit said that investigators in June obtained information from several farms and financial records identifying the supplier of the substance and animal feed containing it to farms.
Officials discovered that after a series of searches conducted on June 11, the suspect transferred more than 8 million baht out of his accounts.
Investigators subsequently gathered further evidence, including witness statements, financial records and scientific test results, to identify the substance found at the farms.
Laboratory tests confirmed it was salbutamol. Investigators then submitted the evidence to the court to obtain an arrest warrant.
On Sept 4, police arrested the suspect, identified only as “Mr Ek”, at his home. A background check found that he had worked as a sales representative in the animal-feed industry since 1996, although he currently did not hold a licence to sell feed.
An examination of accounts associated with animal-feed transactions found more than 80 million baht flowing into and out of the accounts from late last year until the period when the suspect transferred funds out.

items.title: AC condensation, undersized screws caused parliament ceiling collapse
items.summary: Water dripping from air conditioning ducts and undersized screws used in ceiling panels caused the ceiling of the cafeteria at the parliament complex in Bangkok to collapse on Sunday, an inspection has found.
items.body_text:
Water dripping from air conditioning ducts and undersized screws used in ceiling panels caused the ceiling of the cafeteria at the parliament complex in Bangkok to collapse on Sunday, an inspection has found.
Public works officials who carried out the inspection at the cafeteria on the B2 level concluded that condensation on AC ducts caused water to drip onto the ceiling panels and they collapsed after prolonged absorption, Parliament President Sophon Zaram said on Tuesday.
As well, he said, the screws used to secure the panels were too small. The officials recommended using bigger screws to improve the load-bearing capacity of the panels.
There was no problem with the overall structure and workers would be able to replace the ceiling panels and frames beneath the AC ducts, Mr Sophon said.
Prof Amorn Pimanmas, president of the Structural Engineers Association of Thailand, said on Monday that water leaking and accumulated humidity from water pipes and AC ducts could soften and overload ceiling panels.
He also recommended that humidity-proof panels and screws of suitable size could help prevent the collapse.
The cafeteria was closed on Sunday when the incident occurred so no one was injured. In addition to serving officials and staff, the cafeteria is sometimes used by groups of students on field trips at the parliament, said an official.
The Sappaya-Sapasathan building was built by Sino-Thai Engineering and Construction Plc, which is controlled by the family of Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul, although he no longer has any ties to the company.
The construction contract was awarded in 2013 and the building was originally scheduled to open in late 2015. However, the company had to seek numerous extensions and the budget ballooned from 13 billion baht to 24 billion baht.
The building was finally opened in August 2019 for parliamentary meetings but it was not formally handed over to the government until July 2024.
Ever since the building opened, there have been numerous complaints, including leaking roofs, faulty water pipes, and in some cases, some materials that were not specified in the contracts.

items.title: 'Hands off Koh Kut': Thailand stands firm at UN maritme talks
items.summary: Thailand has made its position clear during maritime border talks with Cambodia under the UN law of the sea - Koh Kut is not part of the reconciliation process.
items.body_text:
Thailand has made its position clear during maritime border talks with Cambodia under the UN law of the sea - Koh Kut is not part of the reconciliation process.
Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow said in his opening statement on Tuesday that the meeting should be limited only the maritime boundary dispute between Thailand and Cambodia, and land borders should be excluded from the hearing.
"This conciliation process does not concern sovereignty over land, which includes the island of Koh Kut," the minister said. "Thailand rejects Cambodia's 1972 continental shelf claim line, which is without legal basis,"
Koh Kut is an island district in Trat province, in the eastern Gulf of Thailand, bordering Cambodia. Cambodia unilaterally claimed its continental shelf line in 1972 and included Koh Kut.
Mr Sisasak said on several occasions before the meeting of the Conciliation Commission that any maritime demarcation would clearly show the island belongs to Thailand.
The panel was set up under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea to seek a solution to the dispute between Thailand and Cambodia. The meeting is in Singapore and will conclude on Wednesday.

items.title: Thailand accuses Cambodia of playing victim as maritime dispute reaches international mediation
items.summary: SINGAPORE, Sept 15 — Thailand accused Cambodia yesterday of playing the victim in a dispute over mariti...
items.body_text:
SINGAPORE, Sept 15 — Thailand accused Cambodia yesterday of playing the victim in a dispute over maritime resources, as the Southeast Asian neighbours took their feud to international mediators a year after deadly clashes over their land border.
Cambodia, which initiated the case before the Permanent Court of Arbitration (PCA) in Singapore, said it hoped the hearings would yield a peaceful resolution for both countries.
In May this year, Thailand unilaterally pulled out of a bilateral framework agreement that aimed to resolve overlapping maritime border claims, but denied any link to their land dispute.
Cambodia subsequently initiated a UN-backed conciliation process at the PCA, saying it hoped to return to constructive negotiations.
Presenting Bangkok’s case before a five-member panel of international legal experts, Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow said Cambodia sought to “vilify Thailand through false narratives, distortion of facts, and unfounded accusations... including at international forums”.
“It does this by playing the role of a victim with a sense of self-righteousness aimed at claiming the moral high ground,” he said.
Last year’s clashes in July and December left dozens of people dead and displaced more than a million before a truce was agreed.
Thailand has said it withdrew from the framework agreement, called “MoU 44”, because “no progress had been made” in implementing it. Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul denied the move was linked to the fighting.
The 2001 memorandum of understanding covers a resource-rich maritime territory of around 27,000 square kilometres (10,500 square miles) to which both Cambodia and Thailand lay claim.
Rebuild trust
Cambodia said last week that it had resorted to conciliation “after Thailand unilaterally terminated the agreed bilateral framework” through which the two nations had “negotiated their overlapping maritime claims for more than two decades”.
Prime Minister Hun Manet said in June that the move was also to “protect Cambodia’s sovereignty and maritime rights in accordance with international law”.
Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn told the PCA panel today that Phnom Penh saw the process “as a means to rebuild trust, not as a form of escalation”.
Cambodia’s goal was to agree with Thailand on a “single, all-purpose maritime boundary”, or alternatively agree to jointly develop and equitably share resources until a boundary is drawn, he said.
“Our overriding objective is to achieve a resolution that serves the people of both nations and contribute to peace, cooperation, and share prosperity in the region,” Prak Sokhonn said.
“Cambodia sincerely hopes that Thailand will engage constructively in this process,” he added.
Despite his rhetoric, Sihasak said Thailand was also seeking maritime delimitation and to rebuild trust.
“Thailand stands ready to engage in this process constructively with the aim of achieving with the commission’s assistance a negotiated and equitable solution,” the Thai foreign minister said.
Analysts have said that both Thailand’s withdrawal from the 2001 MOU and Cambodia’s conciliation case were driven by domestic political calculations.
Set up in 1899, the PCA is the world’s oldest intergovernmental dispute-resolution body and resolves issues between countries and private parties by referring to contracts, special agreements and various treaties, such as the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea.
The PCA office in Singapore is the Hague-based court’s first in Asia.
The commission’s recommendations are not binding and will take about a year to be decided. — AFP

items.title: China warns US against space arms race after Space Force deploys weapons in orbit
items.summary: BEIJING, Sept 15 — China urged the United States today to “stop preparing for war” in space...
items.body_text:
BEIJING, Sept 15 — China urged the United States today to “stop preparing for war” in space, after the US Space Force confirmed it had deployed weapons into orbit for the first time.
Beijing and Washington are key geopolitical rivals and have long sought to expand their interests—and strategic footprints—in space.
The US Space Force said yesterday that it had deployed “on-orbit space control weapons capable of defending... against hostile adversary action”, without providing specifics.
China’s foreign ministry opposed the move, warning against the “weaponisation of outer space, turning it into a battlefield, as well as an arms race there”.
“We urge the US side to stop expanding its military capabilities and preparing for war in outer space,” ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun told a news briefing.
The US Space Force singled out China as a threat in its announcement, saying Beijing “develops and operates space and counterspace capabilities as part of a military modernization strategy”.
It also named Russia, another geopolitical rival, which it said “believes space supremacy will be a decisive factor in future conflicts”.
The militarisation of space is as old as the space race itself—as soon as the Soviet Union launched the world’s first artificial satellite, Sputnik, into orbit in 1957, Washington and Moscow began exploring ways to both arm and destroy such spacecraft.
The biggest worry was once about nuclear weapons in space, but the superpowers and other countries signed the Outer Space Treaty in 1967, banning weapons of mass destruction in orbit.
Since then, the United States, China, Russia and India have explored ways to fight in space outside of that treaty, including by targeting rivals’ satellites, which are key for military communications, surveillance and navigation. — AFP

items.title: WTO warns of 'most serious and sustained' trade disruptions
items.body_text:
WTO warns of 'most serious and sustained' trade disruptions
The WTO pointed to a range of factors that have hit cooperation, including shifts in economic power and the growing prominence and diversity of government intervention in markets.
GENEVA: The global trading system is enduring its most sustained disruption in living memory amid challenges to trading rules that could batter living standards in a "geo-fragmented world", the WTO warned on Tuesday (Sep 15).
The system is now in a decisive phase, the World Trade Organization said in its annual report, which "provides new evidence that a reversion to unilateral trade policy would impose large costs".
Such a reversal could slash global GDP by around five per cent and drag down exports 18.6 per cent by 2050, it warned.
"Global trade policy and the WTO are experiencing the most serious and sustained disruptions since the multilateral trading system was created 80 years ago," the report said.
It echoed a warning by its director general Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala in March, shortly after the start of the US-led war on Iran.
"We have seen trade rules challenged on a scale unseen since multilateral institutions were created to underpin open, stable and predictable global trade in the wake of the Great Depression and the Second World War," Okonjo-Iweala wrote in a preface to the report.
She said trade cooperation had "helped narrow income gaps between developing and advanced economies, and contributed to peace among members".
Although "the global trading landscape has changed significantly ... the founding logic of the system, that all economies are better off cooperating rather than acting unilaterally, remains as relevant today as ever", she added.
"SAFEGUARD WHAT WORKS"
But the outlook has darkened after US President Donald Trump launched a tariff blitz since returning to the White House in January 2025, and amid soaring geopolitical tensions, particularly in the Middle East.
The WTO pointed to a range of factors that have hit cooperation, including shifts in economic power and the growing prominence and diversity of government intervention in markets.
Looking forward, WTO economists analysed the likely economic growth development under different scenarios.
They found that "fragmentation along geopolitical lines could reduce global GDP by about five per cent", Okonjo-Iweala told diplomats onTuesday.
And "in a world where the WTO disappears and is replaced by a network of FTAs [free trade agreements], the losses would be closer to seven per cent", she warned.
Moreover, the costs of any erosion of multilateral trade would not be born equally, as the smallest and poorest economies would be particularly vulnerable.
"In contrast, if members act purposefully to reinforce multilateral trade cooperation, safeguard what works, reform what doesn't, it could boost global GDP by roughly three per cent," Okonjo-Iweala said.
GROWING RESTRICTIONS
The WTO, which will unveil an update to its global trade forecasts on Oct 8, remains the linchpin of the rules-based global trading system, with a full 72 per cent of global trade still operating under its rules.
"At the same time, two years ago, that share stood at 80 per cent," the agency's chief economist, Robert Staiger, told AFP, acknowledging that "the trend is disturbing".
"Another sign that global trade is coming under pressure is that new tariffs and trade restrictions now cover 11 per cent of global imports, and that represents the highest coverage in over 15 years," he said.
While global trade figures remain quite strong, Staiger suggested artificial intelligence was helping to shore up the system.
"We also need to acknowledge that some of the resilience may be reflecting AI and the AI boom and the fact that AI-enabling goods are extremely trade intensive," he said.
"There's a lot of imports that go into producing AI enabling goods like servers and factories and computers and data centres, and that investment boom ... may be masking some of the drop

items.title: Bad weather hampers Indonesia ferry rescue, dozens still missing
items.summary: "We cannot fight nature; the swells and waves in the area were extremely high," said the national search and rescue agency, Basarnas.
items.body_text:
Bad weather hampers Indonesia ferry rescue, dozens still missing
"We cannot fight nature; the swells and waves in the area were extremely high," said the national search and rescue agency, Basarnas.
BANJARMASIN, Indonesia: Indonesian rescuers brought ashore on Tuesday (Sep 15) nearly two dozen survivors from a passenger ship that capsized off Java island at the weekend, their evacuation delayed by bad weather, officials said.
Dozens of people remain unaccounted for three days after the Virgo Transport 8, which carried 213 passengers and 30 crew, went down early Sunday.
Six people have died while a total of 108 have been rescued alive and 129 others are still missing, the national search and rescue agency, Basarnas, said in a statement Tuesday. The death toll and the missing figure have remained unchanged since Sunday.
The ferry had lost contact with its shipping company shortly after departing from Indonesia's second-largest city of Surabaya on Java island, headed for Banjarmasin on Borneo.
Footage released by the rescue agency on Monday showed the capsized vessel with a part of the hull visible above the waterline.
Basarnas said that 22 survivors were brought to a harbour in Banjarmasin on Tuesday, after bad weather had prevented their rescue a day earlier.
"The plan was to evacuate them to Trisakti Port yesterday, but adverse weather conditions prevented us from doing so," local search and rescue agency head I Putu Sudayana told reporters.
"We cannot fight nature; the swells and waves in the area were extremely high."
Four bodies were also airlifted to Banjarmasin Tuesday, Basarnas said.
Nearly 1,100 rescuers, including from the navy and police, were involved in the search operation, which also included more than a dozen vessels and five aircraft, the agency said.
Marine accidents are a regular occurrence in Indonesia, an archipelago of more than 17,000 islands that relies heavily on boat connections for daily transport and tourism.
Lax safety standards and unpredictable weather are the main reasons for the disasters.

items.title: Grab takes majority stake in Atome Financial in US$1.49 billion deal
items.summary: Grab will take an initial 60 per cent stake in Atome for US$1.49 billion, combining the target's Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL) loans, consumer cash loans, BNPL cards and digital lending with its own financial services business.
items.body_text:
Grab takes majority stake in Atome Financial in US$1.49 billion deal
Grab will take an initial 60 per cent stake in Atome for US$1.49 billion, combining the target's Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL) loans, consumer cash loans, BNPL cards and digital lending with its own financial services business.
Singapore's Grab said on Tuesday (Sep 15) that it will acquire Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL) provider Atome Financial in a deal that could ultimately value the target at up to US$4.5 billion, boosting its push into Southeast Asian consumer lending.
Grab will take an initial 60 per cent stake in Singapore-based Atome for US$1.49 billion, combining the target's BNPL loans, consumer cash loans, BNPL cards and digital lending with its own financial services business, the ride-hailing and delivery firm said.
The company also agreed to acquire the remaining 40 per cent stake about two years after the transaction closes under a performance-linked framework tied to Atome's EBITDA and revenue, with the valuation capped at US$4.5 billion and floored at US$2 billion.
The transaction is expected to complete by the third quarter of 2027.
"Subject to closing timelines, we expect Atome Financial, along with the rest of our Financial Services segment, to generate an adjusted EBITDA of US$500 million by 2028 with a combined gross loan portfolio of over US$6 billion," said Peter Oey, CFO of Grab.
He added that Grab is also lifting its 2028 targets to US$1.7 billion in adjusted EBITDA and annual revenue growth above 30 per cent between 2025 and 2028.

PHILADELPHIA – In the middle of cascading fears of artificial intelligence running amok and one day posing grave danger to human society, President Donald Trump has made a clear choice: the US must not slow down.
“Whoever wins AI, wins,” Trump said, defying calls from the tech industry leaders to regulate cutting-edge AI for the sake of safety and framing the choice as a geopolitical question of beating China.
“We’re leading China in AI. We’re the most sophisticated country in the world, and frankly I want to keep it that way,” he told reporters during a trip to Ireland.
In a flurry of comments and social media posts, he has also scoffed at the world’s most influential AI companies, dismissing their concerns as “a hoax”.
The only safeguard the nation needs is a “strong and smart (high IQ) president,” he said on Truth Social.
The question of regulating AI came to the fore after Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei, the developer of Claude AI, warned in unusually specific terms on Sept 12 that AI could be capable within six to twelve months of coordinating swarms of autonomous agents powerful enough to take over the internet.
It was time to stop competing for technical supremacy, accept outside scrutiny and jointly slow down to focus more on safety before going any further, Amodei said in a lengthy essay.
Voluntary action by a single company would not be enough, he said, asking for safety standards coordinated among democratic governments and for negotiations with “authoritarian powers” like China.
Competitors back call for AI slowdown
Against the backdrop of a series of hacks in recent months that showed AI agents can conspire to deceive humans, Amodei’s call gained surprising support from some of his biggest rivals – OpenAI’s Sam Altman and Google DeepMind’s Demis Hassabis. xAI’s Elon Musk and Microsoft’s Satya Nadella also indicated agreement.
As the idea of a slowdown began trending, Trump spoke louder. He questioned the acumen of the tech CEOs calling for government oversight. “When, in the history of business, did anyone see the leaders of an industry call for regulation that, if strongly implemented, will drive them into oblivion and bankruptcy?” he said on social media.
“It’s a hoax,” he insisted in a live five-minute phone call with Nvidia chief Jensen Huang who was speaking at a Sept 14 conference in Los Angeles.
“The robots are not going to be taking over the world. That’s not going to happen.”
Huang, who heads the world’s top company designing advanced AI chips, is on the other side of the debate and has dismissed AI risks as overblown.
Trump’s former AI czar David Sacks, the Silicon Valley investor who has shaped much of the administration’s AI policy, also reacted with hostility. Posting on social media, he said Amodei’s call smacked of “regulatory capture” or an attempt to seal in an early mover advantage through rules that leave newer rivals hobbled.
AI companies can choose to act responsibly on their own, he wrote on X.
“If the unreleased models are scary enough that you think you should slow down, I support your decision to be responsible. But stop pretending you need anyone else’s permission,” he posted on Sept 13.
“Most of all, stop pretending the motivation to slow down is purely altruistic. You face massive product-liability exposure if your products enable a truly damaging cyberattack.

items.title: Italian Senate clears Meloni's electoral reform amid opposition resistance
items.summary: ROME, Sept 15 - A contested reform of Italy's electoral law won Senate approval on Tuesday amid fierce opposition criticism, as rivals accused Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni of changing the rules to improve her chances of winning re-election next year.
items.body_text:
Italian Senate clears Meloni's electoral reform amid opposition resistance
ROME, Sept 15 - A contested reform of Italy's electoral law won Senate approval on Tuesday amid fierce opposition criticism, as rivals accused Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni of changing the rules to improve her chances of winning re-election next year.
Meloni's conservative coalition, including Brothers of Italy, the League and Forza Italia, has put forward a fully proportional voting system that would guarantee a parliamentary majority to any alliance winning more than 42% of the vote.
The measure still needs final approval from Italy's lower house.
Under the current system, most lawmakers are elected through proportional representation, while a third are chosen in first-past-the-post constituencies that analysts say may favour the centre-left opposition. The reform would abolish these.
The coalition said the reform, approved by 113 votes to 71, would ensure political stability in a country notorious for short-lived governments. Meloni took office in 2022 and this month became the leader of Italy's longest-lasting administration since World War Two.
"This isn't about stability. You're doing it because you believe that there is a risk you will lose the next election," said former prime minister Matteo Renzi, leader of the Italia Viva party.
LAW GOES BACK TO LOWER HOUSE
After the vote, centre-left senators waved red and yellow placards bearing the slogan: "No to the fraud law."
The reform's initial approval in the lower house in July was overshadowed by a setback for Meloni. Her proposal to reintroduce preferential voting — which allows voters to pick their preferred candidates from party lists — was narrowly defeated in a secret ballot due to defections within the ruling coalition.
That vote exposed strains within the alliance ahead of an election due next year, fuelling perceptions that Meloni's grip on the coalition may be weakening at a time when the centre-left holds a narrow lead in the polls.
Rather than drop the measure, Meloni, who has long supported preferential voting, brought it back to the Senate, which approved it. Because the reform was amended, it must now return to the Chamber of Deputies, or lower house, for a final vote.
Some politicians suggest the new law could benefit Meloni's opponents, who could surpass the 42% threshold and secure the majority bonus, while a new far-right party, National Future, steadily erodes support for her conservative coalition.
Meloni has rejected the suggestion she might make an electoral pact with National Future, but polls say such a tie-up would give them a clear lead over the centre-left bloc.
The reform would also require each alliance to name its candidate for prime minister before the election, a provision that is deepening tensions among the leaders of the fractious opposition parties.
"That could prove problematic for the centre-left, potentially forcing an early leadership contest and exposing divisions that could weaken the bloc," said Rado Fonda, of pollster SWG. REUTERS

  - By Hollie Younger / Staff writer, with CNA
 Lithuanian lawmaker Dovile Sakaliene over the weekend urged Taiwan to prioritize its defense budget, saying that national security cannot be compromised for other public policies, during a joint conference of Taiwanese associations in Helsinki. She made the comments at this year’s Joint Annual Meeting of the World Federation of Taiwanese Associations and the European Federation of Taiwanese Associations, which took place from Friday to Sunday. The event, themed “Democratic Resilience and Trusted Democracy,” drew more than 330 participants, including politicians and human rights advocates from Taiwan, Finland, Lithuania, Poland and the UK, to discuss how democratic societies can resist legal, diplomatic and military coercion by authoritarian states. Attendees pose for a photograph in front of a banner reading “Democratic Resilience & Trusted Solidarity” during the joint annual conference of the World Federation of Taiwanese Associations and the European Federation of Taiwanese Associations in Helsinki over the weekend.Photo: CNA “Taiwan and Ukraine are the structural safety pins of global stability. Pull them and the whole transatlantic system unzips,” Sakaliene wrote on social media yesterday. “Vilnius and Taipei are not two separate stories. Russia and China are one problem working two fronts, and whichever of us folds first makes taking the other one cheaper,” she added. Sakaliene served as Lithuania’s minister of national defense from December 2024 to October last year, when she stepped down following disputes over increasing defense spending. She gave a presentation over the weekend titled: “Resilience Under Pressure: Lessons from Lithuania and NATO’s Eastern Flank,” and participated in the panel “Frontline Democracies — Geopolitical Resilience in an Era of Authoritarian Pressure.” Taiwan must invest sufficient resources to maintain its self-defense capabilities, as China’s military aircraft and exercises have become the “new normal,” she said. If you cannot protect your country, then who would be left to benefit from education spending, she asked, adding that if nations do not strengthen their own military, they are only strengthening that of the enemy. As cooperation grows between China, Russia, Iran and North Korea, Taiwan faces a similar situation to Europe, she said. There are no shortcuts to democratic resilience; it is built day by day through strengthening social trust, maintaining defense capabilities and ensuring that democratic institutions can continue functioning during a crisis, said Atte Harjanne, member of the Finnish parliament and First Vice Chair of the Taiwan Friendship Group. items.title: VP praises Taiwan’s visibility, nations’ attention
items.body_text:

            VP praises Taiwan’s visibility, nations’ attentionPLEDGE: Europe and Taiwan would remain steadfast in upholding a free and democratic way of life and maintaining regional peace and prosperity, Hsiao said
  - Staff writer, with CNA
 Vice President Hsiao Bi-khim (蕭美琴) yesterday said that she saw a growing number of international friends willing to learn about Taiwan and hear its story during her visit to the Italian island of Ventotene last week. “Throughout this journey, I have once again felt the international community’s concern for Taiwan, and encountered a growing number of good friends willing to learn about Taiwan and hear its story,” Hsiao said at Taiwan Taoyuan International Airport upon returning from Italy. The most significant part of the trip was “having Taiwan’s voice heard by so many more people in a place of such historical significance,” Hsiao said, referring to the Second Ventotene European Conference for Freedom and Democracy, which she attended last week. Vice President Hsiao Bi-khim, seated, third left, and Minister of Foreign Affairs Lin Chia-lung, seated, fourth left, attend a dinner hosted by European Parliament Vice President Pina Picierno on the Italian island of Ventotene on Friday.Photo courtesy of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Hsiao said that Ventotene has an extraordinary history. During World War II, the island was used to detain political dissidents, including Altiero Spinelli, who coauthored a text there that later became known as the Ventotene Manifesto, advocating a federal Europe after the war. Hsiao cited remarks from her Friday address at the Italian conference, saying: “Whether it is Ventotene or Taiwan, no island is too small to have a voice, and no island or society is too small to deserve respect.” Although Europe today is vastly different from the Europe of World War II, democracies around the world continue to face similar challenges, she said. “Authoritarianism, ‘gray zone’ threats, and challenges involving coercion and attempts to alter the ‘status quo’ continue to arise in various forms and locations — challenges with which Taiwan is all too familiar,” she said. Hsiao said that is why she told at the conference that Taiwan, like its European friends, would remain steadfast in upholding a free and democratic way of life, and committed to maintaining regional peace and prosperity. The trip was not announced in advance to avoid “unnecessary interference,” she said, referring to China’s objections. Hsiao was invited by European Parliament Vice President Pina Picierno, the main initiator of the conference, and Carlo Corazza, head of the European Parliament Liaison Office in Italy, to speak at the meeting, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs said in a news release yesterday. Aside from meeting Picierno and Corazza, Hsiao and Minister of Foreign Affairs Lin Chia-lung (林佳龍) also met with Sandro Gozi, chair of the European Parliament’s Delegation to the EU-UK Parliamentary Partnership Assembly; European Parliament member Valerie Hayer; and Ventotene Mayor Carmine Caputo while on the Italian island. Before returning to Taiwan, Hsiao and Lin toured the renowned Roman cisterns and the Museo Storico Archeologico, which houses archeological discoveries from the island, the ministry said.

items.title: SkyGuardian drones bought from US tested, source says
items.body_text:
- 
            SkyGuardian drones bought from US tested, source says
  - Staff writer, with CNA
 The first two of the four MQ-9B “SkyGuardian” drones Taiwan purchased from the US underwent their first flight tests at an air base in eastern Taiwan early yesterday, a source familiar with the matter said. The unnamed source did not disclose further details about the test flights, saying that they were conducted at Hualien Air Base. The tests were conducted after the military and the drone manufacturer completed the assembly of the two drones delivered to Taiwan earlier this year, the source added. An MQ-9B drone taxis at Hualien Air Base yesterday. A retired F-5E jet serving as a decoy aircraft is visible in the background.Photo: Yu Tai-lang, Taipei Times On March 17, Deputy Minister of National Defense Hsu Szu-chien (徐斯儉) and Representative to the US Alexander Yui (俞大?) attended a handover ceremony in the US for two of the MQ-9Bs. The US has agreed to deliver the four MQ-9Bs to Taiwan in two batches this year and next year. The MQ-9Bs would provide Taiwan with “intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance, target acquisition, and counter-land, counter-sea and anti-submarine strike capabilities,” according to the US Defense Security Cooperation Agency. Su Tzu-yun (蘇紫雲), a research fellow at the government-funded Institute for National Defense and Security Research (INDSR), previously said that the role of the MQ-9Bs in Taiwan is to enhance battlefield reconnaissance and surveillance capabilities rather than serve as a primary offensive weapon. INDSR researcher Hsieh Pei-shiue (謝沛學) wrote in 2020, when the US first approved the sale to Taiwan, that the drone is capable of linking to satellite communications networks shared among US allies. That means Taiwan and the US could share battlefield intelligence instantly, providing opportunities for the two sides to cooperate during a conflict. For example, if a cross-strait conflict breaks out, Washington could take advantage of anti-ship missile systems deployed along the First Island Chain to prevent Chinese People’s Liberation Army vessels from sailing into waters east of Taiwan to blockade the nation, Hsieh said. MQ-9Bs are capable of long-term, long-range surveillance, meaning the drones could fly near Chinese vessels and provide critical intelligence for US forces to target them, Hsieh wrote at the time. Another INDSR researcher, Kao Chih-jung (高志榮), yesterday cautioned that while the MQ-9B can detect and classify a large number of targets at once, it still requires final visual identification by human operators. That limits the drone to conducting detailed, continuous surveillance on only two or three targets simultaneously, Kao said. Consequently, the military should not rely solely on a handful of large drones, but should instead utilize the MQ-9B to conduct wide-area scans and designate high-value targets, he said. That intelligence could then be distributed to small and medium-sized drones, shore-based radars and other combat units to build a more resilient “integrated reconnaissance and strike” network, he added. items.title: NGO concerned about South China Morning Post reporter Minnie Chan, 3 years after apparent disappearance
items.summary: Free expression NGO Reporters Without Borders (RSF) has expressed concern over the apparent disappearance of South China Morning Post (SCMP) reporter Minnie Chan close to three years ago. Chan reported on defence issues, but was last heard from in October 2023 while she was covering the Xiangshan Forum, a three-day security conference, in Beijing. The […]
items.body_text:
Free expression NGO Reporters Without Borders (RSF) has expressed concern over the apparent disappearance of South China Morning Post (SCMP) reporter Minnie Chan close to three years ago.
Chan reported on defence issues, but was last heard from in October 2023 while she was covering the Xiangshan Forum, a three-day security conference, in Beijing.
The French NGO said that there has been no news of the whereabouts of the award-winning reporter since: “Various RSF sources in China also believe Minnie Chan is being held by the Chinese regime under charges which they say have not been publicly disclosed but appear to be national-security-related, and that she is facing at least 10 years in prison. RSF could not verify this information or find clear evidence of her detention,” they said in a Tuesday press release.
Aleksandra Bielakowska, advocacy manager at RSF’s Asia-Pacific office, said that Chan’s “whereabouts must be made public, and the international community must do everything in its power to secure the release of this talented journalist, who does not belong in a Chinese prison.”
When asked about Chan in 2023, China’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson Wang Wenbin said: “I’m not aware of that [situation].”
SCMP silent
RSF said it approached the SCMP “requesting information about Chan’s current employment status, confirmation of her detention and the nature of any charges, as well as information about what support is being provided to the journalist in the event she is detained. At the time of publication, the SCMP had not replied.”
SCMP did not respond to HKFP’s enquiries on Tuesday. It threatened legal action over HKFP’s initial coverage of Chan’s apparent disappearance, without disputing the reporting.
At the time, the paper said the safety of journalists was of utmost importance and that it had no further information to disclose.
According to RSF, China is the “world’s largest prison for journalists,” with over 100 currently behind bars.
Chinese Bloomberg journalist Haze Fan disappeared in 2020 in China but was released on bail in 2022. Cheng Lei, an Australian journalist, was held in China in 2020 and released in 2023. In 2015, Hong Kong bookseller Gui Minhai disappeared in Thailand before being imprisoned in China.

items.title: Education University PhD student gets 160 hours of community service over doctored reference
items.summary: A mainland Chinese woman has been handed a 160-hour community service order after pleading guilty to forging a reference letter for her application to a doctoral programme at a Hong Kong university. Li Zuer, who faced a charge of obtaining services by deception, appeared at the Fanling Magistrates’ Courts on Monday. The court heard earlier […]
items.body_text:
A mainland Chinese woman has been handed a 160-hour community service order after pleading guilty to forging a reference letter for her application to a doctoral programme at a Hong Kong university.
Li Zuer, who faced a charge of obtaining services by deception, appeared at the Fanling Magistrates’ Courts on Monday.
The court heard earlier that she had commissioned an agent to rewrite a reference letter for a doctoral programme at the Education University of Hong Kong, after previously failing to gain admission, local media reported.
According to the prosecution, she submitted a doctored letter – dated March 2024 – based on a reference that was written for her by Ho Wai-yip, a former associate professor at the Education University who taught her when she was studying for a master’s degree there.
The letter stated that Li’s English proficiency could be improved. The edited version was rewritten to state that Li’s academic performance was exceptional.
Li was admitted to the university, studying international and comparative education. She has since lost her place at the school.
Handing down the sentence, magistrate Kenneth Chan said the case was serious as Li could have robbed another applicant of their chance for enrolment, The Witness reported.
But he said he took into account the defence’s evidence that Li had strong academic results and was devoted to teaching, and committed the offence because she was influenced by her agent.
Li’s mother submitted a mitigation letter to the court stating that her daughter had always been an honest person and felt remorseful about her offence.
Chan said that while imprisonment was a viable punishment for her case, he had decided to give her a chance and sentenced her to community service instead.

items.title: Yuen Long district councillor convicted of having intercourse with girl under 16
items.summary: A Yuen Long district councillor has been found guilty of having intercourse with a girl under 16 over a decade ago, prompting a government investigation that could see him suspended from duties. Sei Chun-hing was convicted at the District Court on Monday following the conclusion of his trial in July. He was charged with having […]
items.body_text:
A Yuen Long district councillor has been found guilty of having intercourse with a girl under 16 over a decade ago, prompting a government investigation that could see him suspended from duties.
Sei Chun-hing was convicted at the District Court on Monday following the conclusion of his trial in July. He was charged with having intercourse with a girl under 16 and indecent assault, but was acquitted of the latter charge.
The case revolved around two incidents involving a girl, known to the court as X, in 2008 and 2011. X told the court that she met Sei through a school event, local media reported.
Sei was accused of groping X’s chest when she was aged 11 in Ko Shan Road Park, near her school, in November 2008. During Sei’s testimony, the defendant said that he only met X in December that year, and that they had never been to that park.
The defence summoned a tree expert, who testified that the type of tree found in the background of a photo could not be found at Ko Shan Road Park. The judge therefore cleared him of the indecent assault charge.
According to the prosecution, the intercourse offence involved Sei and X having sex at his residence on March 14, 2011. X was 13 at the time.
Sei denied the accusation. He said he and X had dated, but that they never had sexual intercourse when they were together.
He told the court that his colleagues were at his home for a meeting that day, and that she did not go to his home then.
He said he only met X at Tsuen Wan West MTR station after that, and they went to Tsim Sha Tsui together to have noodles. The defence submitted a photo of the two of them on the MTR together.
Judge Stanley Chan said Sei’s testimony was false, questioning why they did not meet in Tsim Sha Tsui directly.
Chan also raised questions about the photo, saying that the light outside the MTR windows was very bright. While the photo’s metadata indicated that it was shot at close to 7pm, Chan suspected that the information had been altered, local media reported.
Meanwhile, X testified that the photo was not taken on that date. The defence said that all the photo proved was that they had taken the MTR together before.
‘A dangerous person’
A member of the Democratic Alliance for the Betterment and Progress of Hong Kong, the city’s largest pro-Beijing party, Sei was elected to the Yuen Long District Council in 2023.
During the trial, the defence asked X about her sharing of a petition in 2012 against national education, as well as her boyfriend’s posts in 2019 about the anti-extradition protests and unrest.
X reported the incident to police in 2023. Sei’s lawyer suggested that she only did so for political reasons, The Witness reported.
X explained that seeing online posts that Sei was running for the District Council triggered her memory of what had happened between them, so she began recollecting the incident in her mind and she approached Rainlily, an NGO that supports sexual assault victims, for help.
“In his role [as a district councillor], he has many opportunities to go into the community and into schools,” she testified.
“I think he is a dangerous person. I don’t want there to be other victims,” X said.
When asked by Chan if she never would have made the police report if he had not run for District Council, X disagreed. She said she had never forgotten the incidents, and that she was just not ready to face them.
Sei, who was remanded into custody after being convicted, will be sentenced on October 27. He faces up to five years in jail, the maximum imprisonment term for having intercourse with a girl under 16 but over the age of 13.
Investigation underway
Authorities said they will appoint a committee to investigate Sei following the conviction.
“The Government stressed that it places great importance on the conduct and integrity of District Council members. It added that it will closely monitor the ongoing legal proceedings and take appropriate follow-up action,” a government statement on Monday read.

The US is haemorrhaging goodwill around the world, but China will have to build up its own trustworthiness and credibility to win hearts and minds
3-MIN READ3-MIN
Alex Lo has been an SCMP columnist since 2012, commenting on China and international affairs. 
Global surveys show China is now more popular than the United States in most countries. The reality is China hasn’t become more popular, only that Uncle Sam has become odious.
Two recent major summits demonstrate precisely why this erosion has occurred. At the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, and the Group of 20 (G20) gathering in the US, the Trump administration faced withering criticism for policies that have destabilised global commerce, violated international law and alienated even Washington’s closest partners.
The SCO summit, representing organisations that account for roughly 40 per cent of all the people in the world, issued a joint declaration that laid bare the depth of international opposition to American policy.
The Bishkek Declaration condemned “military strikes on the territory of the Islamic Republic of Iran, which have resulted in heavy civilian casualties and significant damage to the country’s economy”, stating that the US-Israeli attacks “violate the principles and norms of international law and the UN Charter and create serious risks to international peace, security and stability”.

Further multi-physics simulations and vehicle-level testing needed before proposed systems could move towards practical deployment
3-MIN READ3-MIN
 Listen
Chao Kongin Beijing
Chinese military researchers have outlined an ambitious plan to develop a nuclear-powered main battle tank armed with an electromagnetic railgun capable of hitting targets up to 450km (280 miles) away, possibly debuting after 2045.
Detailed in a peer-reviewed paper published in June in the Chinese journal Acta Armamentarii, the concept envisions a 60-tonne armoured vehicle driven by a 10-megawatt-class small modular reactor (SMR) and a 50-megajoule (MJ) railgun.
The paper was written by researchers from Inner Mongolia First Machinery Group – part of China’s defence industrial system and closely associated with the development and manufacture of tanks and armoured vehicles – and the Beijing Institute of Technology.
The National Key Laboratory of Special Vehicle Design and Manufacturing Integration Technology funded the study through a special research project.

items.body_text:
面對中國爭奪話語權 台東舉辦「南島文化論壇」展現韌性
台東縣府推廣南島活動，論壇今年邁向第三年。（資料照片，縣府提供）
由台東縣政府主辦的「2026 南島文化論壇」，將於10月13日至15日在國立台灣史前文化博物館舉行，今年主題特別聚焦於「青年的視角」。面對中國近年不僅覬覦台灣主權，更在文化及南島語族話語權上不斷蠶食，活動主辦人、國立台東大學教授葉淑綾表示，這就像賣家都可以自稱是「第一家」，但之後能走出什麼樣的路才是真正的重點，正如即將舉辦的論壇活動所展現的價值。
中國與毛利人、紐澳原住民等南島民族交流並自稱是「南島語族發源地」已有數年。據外賓透露，在今年台東縣府舉行南島文化活動期間，也曾遇過中方前來接洽，顯示海峽兩岸在文化領域上也正展開一場「文化起源」的爭奪。
對此，成功大學考古學研究所創辦人劉益昌曾指出，「人種」與「文化」是不同的概念。若如中國所言南島語族來自中國，「不如說全世界的人都來自非洲」；雖然現代人都帶有非洲智人、尼安德塔人與丹尼索瓦人的血統，但分支演化成南島語族則是近5千年左右的事，且「台灣是南島語族的發源地」已是考古學界的共識。
除了考古學界的論證，文化界則選擇從現代實踐著手。已邁入第3年的「南島文化論壇」今年更具特色，重點探討南島新世代如何運用傳統生態知識與柔韌的行動力，回應全球氣候變遷與永續發展的挑戰。本次論壇更特別導入曾於聯合國氣候大會採用的「Talanoa Dialogues（塔拉諾亞對話）」，這項源自斐濟的傳統精神，強調南島語族不分尊卑、圍圈坐下平等交談，藉此務實且平等地討論出各項議題心得與未來方向。
葉淑綾教授強調，如何走出屬於南島語族自己的路才是關鍵，正如每個商販都能宣稱自己是「第一家」，但如何推出優質產品並持續走下去更為重要。劉益昌教授也補充，台灣與中國的不同之處在於「我們不會要求別人『認祖歸宗』」，每個文化雖然有脈絡可循，卻又非常重要且各自獨立。
本次論壇核心討論共分為四大項目：首先，探討從在地造舟實務，一路延伸拉升至跨國界的海洋與文化外交行動；其次，研究如何將編織工藝、藝術策展創作以及日常相互照顧的實踐，轉化為當代社會的療癒力量；再者，關注青年如何打破城鄉刻板印象，透過聲景採集、語言復振等多元方式重新錨定文化認同；最後，則是將其轉譯為具備市場韌性的永續旅行與微型產業，藉此支持族人留鄉創業。
台東縣政府文化處處長李吉崇引述玻里尼西亞諺語：「定睛過去、背身轉向未來」，希望讓更多南島民族都能找到屬於自己的未來。台東推動南島文化已長達十多年，期望大家能關注「認同」而非僅著重於「血緣」，從而創造更多人的參與；同時也期盼年輕人能發現這與自己息息相關，並意識到「大家都可以同時是倡議者與行動者」。

items.body_text:
大阪人超狂！1.6噸「脈脈」巨像搭直升機搬家 1400萬人看傻
大阪萬博吉祥物「脈脈」搭乘直升機前往新家。（圖擷取自@nhk_bknews 社群平台「X」）
即便2025年大阪世界博覽會已落幕，官方吉祥物「脈脈」（ミャクミャク）仍舊魅力不減，還數次在社群掀起熱烈話題。近期大阪政府安排「脈脈」前往府內各鄉鎮巡迴展出，還特意派出直升機載運高3.8公尺、重達1.6公噸的脈脈紀念雕像，上演震撼的「高空飛行」，趣味移動畫面迅速吸引全網關注。
綜合日媒報導，以獨特外型風靡全球的脈脈，在大阪世博舉辦期間，場內設置一座高舉雙手比出歡呼姿勢、命名為「興奮雀躍」（wakuwaku）的脈脈紀念雕像。世博結束後，大阪政府決定讓這座雕像前往各地展出，讓更多府民一睹脈脈的魅力，近期預計前往大阪府千早赤阪村自然公園內的「大阪府民之森千早園地」展出。
然而，由於千早園地座落於海拔約1000公尺金剛山山頂，一般車輛無法通行，需要從崎嶇山路的徒步前往，單趟路程得耗時50至70分鐘，傳統陸運方式堪稱不可能的任務。為此，大阪政府決定出動直升機送脈脈一程，日本各大電視台也紛紛安排轉播，紀錄脈脈以空中吊掛方式，進行令人大開眼界的「高空飛行」。
這個高難度移動於昨（14日）下午進行，在各方準備就緒後，直升機將固定在金屬架中的脈脈雕像緩緩拉起，接著逐漸往山頂飛行，期間高舉雙手的脈脈，還在空中隨風輕巧轉向，在起飛約7分鐘後，脈脈順利抵達展出現場，並緩緩降落至地面。報導指出，脈脈預計從9月19日至11月底在此展出，之後再移動到其他場所。
另從大阪府知事吉村洋文分享在社群的影片，只見吉村洋文與其他人在地面迎接脈脈時，險些因直升機降落時的強大風力而站不穩。吉村洋文還在貼文笑說，自己從未想過能親眼見到「飛天脈脈」，也很開心脈脈能平安抵達千早園地，並表示這裡自然風光絕美，邀請民眾不妨來趟初秋登山健行兼朝聖脈脈。
相關影片畫面曝光後，吸引超過1400多萬人次瀏覽，不少日本網友笑喊整個移動過程「很有大阪的風格」，甚至有人形容很像是電影《風之谷》、動畫《烏龍派出所》、特攝劇《超人力霸王》（早期台灣翻譯：鹹蛋超人）等作品會出現的場景。
「ミャクミャク」モニュメントがヘリで大移動
新たな展示場所へhttps://t.co/CJBx5uDzMc#nhk_video pic.twitter.com/guaOrLp6V9
まさか、ミャクミャクが空を飛ぶ日が来るとは思いませんでした。
本日、「ワクワク」ミャクミャクが、大阪で最も高い標高1000mの金剛山、ちはや園地にやってきました。
今週末9月19日（土）に除幕式を行います。
秋の金剛山は自然が素晴らしいです。
1000m地点でミャクミャクが皆さんをお待ちしてます。 pic.twitter.com/gYiFKwM2i1
